entries.old: It is not an entry requirement when arriving from most countries, but vaccination is strongly recommended for the Amazon, the Pantanal, Iguaçu Falls and most inland states, and some countries you travel to afterward will demand the certificate because you have been in Brazil.
entries.new: No, it is not an entry requirement: Brazil's Ministry of Health says no proof of vaccination is required to enter the country. Vaccination is recommended at least 10 days before travel to areas where it is advised, including the Amazon, the Pantanal, Iguaçu Falls and most inland states, and some countries you travel to afterward will demand the certificate because you have been in Brazil.
entries.note: Consistency: said it is not an entry requirement 'when arriving from most countries', implying some arrivals need it; the vaccination entry (Ministry of Health) says no proof of vaccination is required to enter Brazil at all. Aligned with entryRequirements.vaccinations[yellow-fever].

entries.old: A free digital arrival declaration that all foreign visitors must submit online before traveling to Brunei. It replaced the paper disembarkation card — complete it on the Immigration Department's website shortly before your trip.
entries.new: A digital arrival declaration that foreign visitors must submit online before travelling to Brunei: the UK government says it may be requested at check-in, and that you do not need one if you are not passing through immigration. Register on the Immigration Department's portal, imm.gov.bn, then create the card under 'Travel Cards'.
entries.note: Consistency: the FAQ called the card free and said it replaced the paper disembarkation card; neither is stated by the FCDO or Canada, nor in the E-Arrival Card declaration in the data. Rewritten to match that declaration and the FCDO: 'You must submit an e-arrival declaration form to enter Brunei. Do this before you travel as it may be requested at check-in.'

entries.old: Bulgaria is a safe destination overall. Watch for pickpocketing in Sofia and at busy Black Sea resorts, taxi overcharging (use licensed or app-based taxis), and occasional rough road conditions outside main routes.
entries.new: Bulgaria is a safe destination overall. Watch for pickpocketing in Sofia and at busy Black Sea resorts, taxi overcharging (the UK Foreign Office advises official, licensed taxis, and at Sofia airport the official taxi booking office in the arrivals hall), and occasional rough road conditions outside main routes.
entries.note: Consistency: the taxi tip dropped 'app-based taxis' as unsourced; the safety text now gives the FCDO's taxi advice instead.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says terrorist attacks on major roads and transport routes are increasing, including with landmines and other explosive devices, particularly where terrorist groups operate and near border areas.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says attacks on major roads and transport routes by terrorists are increasing, including through the use of landmines and other explosive devices, particularly where terrorist groups operate and near border areas. Canada's travel advice adds that improvised explosive devices pose a real threat on the roads outside Ouagadougou.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct rewrite attributed the UK's sentence to Canada. UK FCDO: "Attacks on major roads and transport routes by terrorists are increasing, including through the use of landmines and other explosive devices." Canada: "Outside the capital, Ouagadougou, improvised explosive devices pose a real threat on the roads."

entries.old: Apart from ECOWAS citizens, who enter freely, visitors to Burkina Faso need a visa arranged in advance through a Burkinabè embassy or the government's online visa service, and most Western governments currently advise against all travel because of widespread jihadist violence.
entries.new: Apart from ECOWAS citizens, who enter freely, visitors to Burkina Faso need a visa arranged in advance through a Burkinabè embassy or the government's online visa service; visas for US citizens are suspended. The UK and Canadian governments advise against all travel because of the threat of terrorism and kidnapping.
entries.note: Consistency: the summary said "most Western governments" advise against all travel, a claim the 3 Oct audit withdrew from the tip and FAQ (only the UK and Canada were confirmed), and it omitted the US row (banned: visas suspended since 30 December 2025).

entries.old: Most Western governments advise against all travel to Burkina Faso. Jihadist groups contest large parts of the country, attacks and kidnapping occur including on main roads, and a state of emergency covers many regions; the situation can change quickly.
entries.new: The UK and Canadian governments advise against all travel to Burkina Faso. Jihadist groups contest large parts of the country, attacks and kidnapping occur including on main roads, and a state of emergency covers many regions; the situation can change quickly.
entries.note: Consistency: "Most Western governments" replaced with the two governments the sources confirm (UK: "FCDO advises against all travel to Burkina Faso"; Canada: "Avoid all travel to Burkina Faso").

entries.old: Each island is distinct and connections take planning: book internal flights and inter-island ferries ahead, and check ferry schedules close to departure.
entries.new: (deleted)
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. The 3 October rewrite was logged as 'rewritten to what official sources state, attributed', but it cites no source, and neither Canada's nor the FCDO's Cabo Verde advice mentions internal flights, inter-island ferries or booking ahead. Tip withdrawn.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says strong currents and powerful waves make swimming dangerous in some places, and that several drownings occur every year, especially in Praia and on Sal. Swim only where locals recommend and heed flag warnings.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says strong currents and powerful waves make swimming dangerous in some places, and that several drownings occur every year, especially in Praia and on Sal. The UK government's travel advice says to follow the lifeguard's instructions and respect the warning flags.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. Canada's sentence ('Several drownings occur every year, especially in Praia and on the island of Sal') is quoted correctly, but 'swim only where locals recommend' is in neither source. Replaced with the FCDO's own advice: 'Follow the lifeguard’s instructions and respect the warning flags.'

entries.old: The Cambodia e-Arrival card is free (UK government). If you arrive by air, complete it at arrival.gov.kh within 7 days before you arrive.
entries.new: The Cambodia e-Arrival card is free. If you arrive by air, complete it within 7 days before you arrive, at arrival.gov.kh or in the official Cambodia e-Arrival app.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG withdrawal. The 3 Oct correction dropped the CeA app as unsourced, but the official portal offers it: arrival.gov.kh "Download Cambodia e-Arrival App Now!" and "Submission is Free." By-air rule per FCDO: "If you are entering Cambodia by air ... you must complete and submit an electronic e-Arrival Card within 7 days prior to your arrival. There is no charge for this."

entries.old: Cambodia issues a 30-day tourist eVisa online (30 USD) and a 30 USD visa on arrival to most nationalities, while ASEAN neighbors enter visa-free. All arrivals are asked to complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival card within 7 days before travel.
entries.new: Cambodia issues a 30-day tourist eVisa online (30 USD) and a 30 USD visa on arrival to most nationalities, while ASEAN neighbors enter visa-free. Travellers arriving by air must complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival card within 7 days before arrival.
entries.note: Consistency: the e-Arrival duty applies to air arrivals (FCDO: "If you are entering Cambodia by air at either Phnom Penh, Siem Reap or Sihanoukville international airports, you must complete..."); the portal only says "All travelers can submit".

entries.old: Cambodia's e-Arrival card combines the immigration, customs and health declarations in one free online form (web or CeA mobile app), submitted within 7 days before arrival. It has replaced the paper forms at the international airports; enforcement at land borders is still uneven — complete it in advance to be safe.
entries.new: Cambodia's e-Arrival card combines the immigration, customs and health declarations in one free online form (web or Cambodia e-Arrival app). Travellers arriving by air at Phnom Penh (Techo), Siem Reap Angkor or Sihanoukville must submit it within 7 days before arrival; the portal says any traveller can submit it.
entries.note: Consistency: "replaced the paper forms" and "enforcement at land borders is still uneven" have no official source. Portal: "All travelers can submit the Cambodia e-Arrival within 7 days before their arrival. Submission is Free."; FCDO for the by-air duty.

entries.old: The Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA) is a free online form combining immigration, customs and health declarations, submitted within 7 days before arrival at arrival.gov.kh or via the CeA app. It replaces the paper arrival forms at the international airports.
entries.new: The Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA) is a free online form combining immigration, customs and health declarations, submitted within 7 days before arrival at arrival.gov.kh or via the Cambodia e-Arrival app. It is required if you arrive by air at Phnom Penh, Siem Reap or Sihanoukville.
entries.note: Consistency: "replaces the paper arrival forms" had no source; replaced with the FCDO by-air requirement.

entries.old: Payable in cash (crisp USD notes) at the border; bring a passport photo. Available at international airports and most land crossings — border officials sometimes ask for unofficial extras at land posts, so insist on the official fee and a receipt.
entries.new: Paid at the border. Available at international airports and major land crossings, but the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Canada's travel advice (updated 26 May 2026) says no photo is needed and the fee can be paid by card, though cash may be needed if electronic systems are down; the UK government's older page asks for a photo and payment in US dollars, so carry both.
entries.note: Consistency: the "unofficial extras at land posts" claim was withdrawn from the tips on 3 Oct as unsourced and is removed here too. Canada: "You can get a tourist or business visa on arrival at international airports and major land border crossings. Photos are not required ... You can use card payment for visa fees but you may need cash if electronic systems are unavailable." FCDO (19 Mar 2026): "You need to provide a photo and pay in US dollars." FCDO/Canada/Smartraveller: land crossings with Thailand closed/suspended.

entries.old: They cost the same (30 USD online or at the border) and both give 30 days. The eVisa skips the arrival line and avoids border overcharging, but it is accepted only at the Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports and the Bavet and Trapeang Kriel land crossings — Cham Yeam and Poipet on the Thai border are temporarily closed to eVisa entry — so check your entry point first.
entries.new: They cost the same (30 USD online or at the border) and both give 30 days. The eVisa is accepted only at the Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports and the Bavet and Trapeang Kriel land crossings — Cham Yeam and Poipet on the Thai border are temporarily closed to eVisa entry — so check your entry point first.
entries.note: Consistency: "avoids border overcharging" repeats the overcharging claim withdrawn on 3 Oct (no official source); "skips the arrival line" also unsourced.

entries.old: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD in cash) at airports and major land borders. Both allow a 30-day stay, extendable once by 30 days.
entries.new: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD) at airports and major land borders; the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Both allow a 30-day stay, extendable once by 30 days.
entries.note: Consistency: "in cash" contradicts Canada ("You can use card payment for visa fees"); added the Thai land-border closure (Canada: "Land border crossings between Cambodia and Thailand are currently closed").

entries.old: Cambodia is generally safe for visitors, but the UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain. Watch for bag-snatching by thieves on motorbikes, especially in Phnom Penh and Sihanoukville, and be alert to scams, including organized-crime compounds advertised as easy, well-paid jobs. Stick to marked paths in remote areas.
entries.new: The UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain; Canada and Australia advise against all travel within 50 km of it, and the land crossings with Thailand are closed. Australia advises a high degree of caution in the rest of the country. Watch for bag-snatching by thieves on motorbikes, and be alert to scams, including organized-crime compounds advertised as easy, well-paid jobs. Stick to marked paths in remote areas.
entries.note: Consistency: "generally safe for visitors" had no source and conflicts with Smartraveller ("exercise a high degree of caution in Cambodia overall"); added Canada "Avoid all travel to the area within 50 kilometres of the Cambodia-Thailand border" and the land-crossing closure.

entries.old: Most visits to Douala, Yaoundé and the coast are trouble-free, but governments advise against travel to the Far North (Boko Haram activity), the Northwest and Southwest regions (armed separatist conflict) and border areas with Chad and the Central African Republic. Petty crime and road accidents are the main everyday risks.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel to the Far-North Region (except around Maroua), the North-West and South-West regions (except Limbé), the Bakassi Peninsula and within 40 km of the borders with Nigeria, Chad and the Central African Republic. It says terrorist attacks could occur anywhere, including Yaoundé and Douala, and that there is a risk of armed robbery and mugging throughout the country; Canada says violent crime occurs frequently, especially at night, in major cities and on main roads.
entries.note: Consistency: 'Most visits to Douala, Yaoundé and the coast are trouble-free' is the reassurance withdrawn from the safety FAQ on 3 October as unsourced; the FCDO says attacks 'could occur anywhere, including major towns and cities such as Yaoundé and Douala'.

entries.old: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Cameroon. Canada's travel advice says the rainy seasons run from mid-March to mid-June and mid-September to mid-November in the central and southern regions, and from mid-January to mid-March and mid-June to mid-September in the north, and that seasonal flooding can make roads impassable.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Cameroon. Canada's travel advice says the rainy seasons run from mid-March to mid-June and mid-September to mid-November in the central and southern regions, and from mid-January to mid-March and mid-June to mid-September in the north, and that seasonal flooding can make roads impassable. The month shown, December, is the only one outside all of these rainy seasons.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — the months kept on 3 October (November, December, January, February) overlap the rainy seasons Canada gives (to mid-November in the south, from mid-January in the north); only December falls outside all of them.

entries.old: Yes. Rapa Nui limits visitors to 30 days and requires a return ticket, a reservation with a registered tourist establishment or an invitation from a Rapa Nui resident, and a completed entry form submitted before departure. The mainland agricultural rules also apply on the flight over.
entries.new: Yes. Rapa Nui limits visitors to 30 days and requires a return ticket, a reservation with a registered tourist establishment or an invitation from a Rapa Nui resident, and a completed entry form submitted before departure.
entries.note: Consistency: "The mainland agricultural rules also apply on the flight over" repeats the customs note withdrawn on 3 Oct (controls on flights to Easter Island), which no official source we read supports. Removed.

entries.old: Every arriving traveler must complete a sworn declaration for the agricultural service (SAG) stating whether they carry food, plants, seeds, wood or animal products. It can be filed online before arrival or on the form handed out on the flight. Undeclared items — including fruit taken from the plane — carry fines that can run into hundreds of US dollars.
entries.new: Every arriving traveler must complete a sworn declaration for the agricultural service (SAG) stating whether they carry food, plants, seeds, wood or animal products. It can be filed online before arrival or on the form handed out on the flight. SAG says that failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.
entries.note: Consistency: the fine "in the hundreds of US dollars" and the fruit-from-the-plane example are not on the cited SAG page and contradicted the customs note and tip rewritten on 3 Oct. SAG: "No declarar productos de riesgo en el formulario de Declaración Jurada SAG está asociado a sanciones y pago de multas."

entries.old: Violent crime against foreigners is rare and cities are generally very safe. Be aware of local laws: authorities enforce them strictly, and Western governments note risks around arbitrary enforcement and exit bans in specific cases.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says serious crime against foreign nationals is relatively rare, but incidents can happen; Canada adds that petty crime such as pickpocketing and phone theft targets foreigners in major cities and tourist areas. Local laws are strictly enforced, and the UK warns that foreign nationals involved in business or civil disputes can be stopped from leaving by an exit ban.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said cities are 'generally very safe', which the cited UK advice does not say ('Serious crime against foreign nationals is relatively rare, but incidents can happen'); Canada says 'Criminals target foreigners, especially in major cities and tourist areas.' Rewritten to the sources.

entries.old: It is not required for regular entry from most countries, but it is strongly recommended for lowland regions and REQUIRED to enter several national parks, including Tayrona and the Amazon. Get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and carry the ICVP certificate.
entries.new: Only if you arrive from certain countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission, when you must show a vaccination certificate. The UK Foreign Office says you may also be asked to show it if you are travelling to areas of Colombia considered high risk, so carry the certificate at all times.
entries.note: Consistency: the park-entry and 10-day claims were withdrawn from the tips as unsupported; the FAQ now matches the vaccinations entry. UK FCDO: 'You may also be asked to show it if you are travelling to areas in Colombia which are considered high risk.'

entries.old: Costa Rica is one of the safer countries in Central America, but petty theft is the main visitor risk — never leave belongings visible in a parked rental car or unattended on a beach. Rip currents cause more tourist deaths than crime; swim only at beaches with lifeguards or ask locally about conditions.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says muggings and theft are significant problems, particularly on the Atlantic coast: watch your valuables on the beach and avoid leaving luggage in a parked car, either in view or in the boot. It adds that gang-related violence, including shootings, has become more frequent in urban areas. Rip currents are very common and there are often no lifeguards, so get reliable local advice before swimming.
entries.note: Consistency: the 'one of the safer countries' and 'rip currents cause more tourist deaths than crime' claims are not in the cited FCDO advice (the rip-current tip was already narrowed on 4 Oct); rewritten to the FCDO's words: 'Muggings and theft are significant problems, particularly on the Atlantic coast' and 'rip currents are very common and there are often no lifeguards'.

entries.old: Yes to both. Croatia joined the Schengen Area and adopted the euro on January 1, 2023, so there are no border checks when arriving from other Schengen countries and prices are in euros.
entries.new: Yes to both. Croatia joined the Schengen Area and adopted the euro on January 1, 2023, so prices are in euros and there are normally no border checks when arriving from other Schengen countries. Checks can still happen: the UK government's travel advice says there are checks at Slovenia's borders with Croatia, and Canada's says Schengen states may temporarily reintroduce internal border controls.
entries.note: Consistency: 'there are no border checks when arriving from other Schengen countries' contradicts the FCDO ('There are checks at Slovenia's borders with Croatia') and Canada (temporary reintroduction of internal controls).

entries.old: The UK FCDO says that if you enter through the north (for example Ercan Airport), the Republic of Cyprus considers you to have entered illegally: you could be fined or prevented from crossing back into the north. Entering through the south, you can use any crossing point to move between north and south.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says that if you enter through the north (for example Ercan Airport), the Republic of Cyprus considers you to have entered illegally: you could be fined, refused entry to or exit from the Republic, or prevented from crossing back into the north. Entering through the south, the FCDO says you can use any crossing point between north and south, but Australia's Smartraveller says non-EU citizens are barred from the Pergamos and Strovilia crossing points, which lie in UK sovereign territory, and will be turned away.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct rewrite said you "can use any crossing point"; that is the FCDO's line for British travellers, but Smartraveller says "Non-EU citizens are barred from travelling through those crossing points [Pergamos and Strovilia] as they're part of the United Kingdom's Sovereign Territory ... you'll be turned away". Narrowed, and completed the FCDO's list ("refused entry to or exit from the Republic of Cyprus").

entries.old: ["Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 liter of spirits, goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air or sea).", "No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country."]
entries.new: ["Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits over 22% (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine); 200 cigarettes (or 250 g of tobacco); and other goods worth up to €300, or €430 by air or sea. Under-17s get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.", "Between EU countries there is no fixed limit on goods for your own use, but Cyprus may set guideline quantities for alcohol and tobacco, which cannot be lower than 800 cigarettes or 10 litres of spirits."]
entries.note: Consistency: the notes omitted the wine and beer allowances and the under-17 rule, and "No limits ... from another EU country" overstated Your Europe, which says each EU country "can set their own guideline values ... These guideline values may not be lower than" 800 cigarettes / 10 litres of spirits. Cyprus is not on the list of countries applying the lower tobacco limit. Same correction as made for Greece on 3 Oct.

entries.note: Consistency: Canada says "Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave from Cyprus"; the Cyprus government's visa page says validity "shall extend at least three months after the intended date of departure from the territory of Cyprus". Ministry wins (hierarchy); Canada recorded as the conflict.

entries.old: Governments advise against all travel to eastern DRC — North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri, where the M23 conflict and other armed groups are active — and the UK also advises against all travel to Haut-Uélé, Maniema, Tanganyika and Haut-Lomami provinces, the Kwamouth territory of Mai-Ndombe and within 50 km of the Central African Republic border. Kinshasa itself sees high crime and occasional unrest; travel with experienced local support.
entries.new: Canada advises against all travel to the DRC, citing the fragile security situation and an Ebola outbreak. The UK advises against all travel to North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uélé, Maniema, Tanganyika and Haut-Lomami provinces, the Kwamouth territory of Mai-Ndombe and within 50 km of the Central African Republic border, where the M23 conflict and other armed groups are active. In Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and other cities the UK says foreign nationals are at particular risk of street robbery.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said 'governments' advise against travel to eastern DRC only, while the tip and FAQ (3 Oct) say Canada advises against all travel to the whole country ('Avoid all travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) due to the fragile security situation and the outbreak of Ebola disease'); the 'travel with experienced local support' advice had no source. Rewritten to Canada and the UK.

entries.old: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Denmark. The CIA World Factbook describes a temperate, humid and overcast climate with mild, windy winters and cool summers.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Denmark; the months shown are not an official recommendation. The CIA World Factbook describes a temperate, humid and overcast climate with mild, windy winters and cool summers.
entries.note: Consistency: the page shows recommended months (May–August) next to 'No official source ... gives a best time'; the text now says the months are not an official recommendation.

entries.old: The UK Foreign Office says the hurricane season normally runs from June to November, and that tropical storms and hurricanes can develop suddenly. Road conditions can deteriorate significantly during and after heavy rain, and the main road from Douglas-Charles Airport is prone to landslides.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the hurricane season normally runs from June to November, and that tropical storms and hurricanes can develop suddenly. Canada's travel advice says road conditions can deteriorate significantly during and after heavy rain, and that the main road from Douglas-Charles Airport is prone to landslides.
entries.note: Audit: the road sentence is Canada's ("Road conditions can deteriorate significantly during and after heavy rains. The main road from Douglas-Charles Airport is prone to landslides"), not the FCDO's; attribution corrected. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: Dominica has low crime and a strong community feel. The real hazards are natural: flash floods, landslides after heavy rain, powerful river currents and remote hiking trails with no phone signal. The island is also directly in the hurricane belt.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the crime rate in Dominica is low, but you could be at risk walking alone away from the main roads, particularly after dark. Canada's travel advice says petty crime such as pickpocketing, purse snatching and theft from vehicles occurs, and that crime typically increases during Carnival and the World Creole Music Festival. The hurricane season runs from June to November.
entries.note: Consistency: the cited FCDO page says "The crime rate in Dominica is low, but you could be at risk walking alone away from the main roads, particularly after dark"; the "strong community feel" and "no phone signal" claims had no source. Canada's crime lines added with attribution. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: Travel with a passport valid for at least six months on arrival. Shorter validity is sometimes accepted for visa-free visitors, but airlines apply the six-month rule at check-in.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Dominica.
entries.note: Consistency: the cited FCDO page says "your passport must have an 'expiry date' at least 6 months after the date you arrive"; the claims that shorter validity is sometimes accepted and that airlines apply the rule at check-in had no source. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from — or having recently transited — a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. No vaccination is required if you fly in directly from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you need a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk; Canada's advice adds that this also applies if you have transited through an airport of such a country.
entries.note: Consistency: FCDO: "you must have a certificate to prove you've had a yellow fever vaccination if you're coming from a country listed as a transmission risk"; Canada: "if you are coming from or have transited through an airport of a country where yellow fever occurs". Removed the unsourced age-1 threshold and "no vaccination needed from the rest of the Caribbean" (WHO lists Trinidad and Tobago as a risk country). Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: Insurance is not an entry condition. The government hospital in Roseau can handle many treatments, but serious cases may need emergency evacuation, so cover that includes medical evacuation is strongly advisable.
entries.new: Insurance is not an entry condition. Canada's travel advice recommends insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays, and says you may have to pay cash immediately for medical treatment.
entries.note: Consistency: the claim about what the Roseau government hospital can handle had no source; replaced with Canada's "Make sure you get travel insurance that includes coverage for medical evacuation and hospital stays" and "You may have to provide immediate cash payment for medical treatment". Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: Yes. Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed onward or return ticket and to give the address where they will stay. Both are commonly asked for at immigration.
entries.new: Yes. Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed onward or return ticket and to give the address where they will stay.
entries.note: Consistency: removed the unsourced claim that both are commonly asked for at immigration; the rest matches onwardTicket. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: The Galápagos has its own charges on top of your flight: Canada's travel advice says you must buy the Galápagos Transit Control Card at the Galápagos Governing Council counter in Quito or Guayaquil airport, and the islands' protected areas charge a separate entrance fee. Budget for both.
entries.new: The Galápagos has its own charges on top of your flight. The Galápagos Governing Council charges USD 20 for the Transit Control Card, bought at its counter in Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in and paid again on every trip. The Galápagos National Park charges foreign tourists an entrance fee of USD 200 (USD 100 under 12, and USD 100 for adult citizens of Andean Community and Mercosur countries). Budget for both.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG withdrawal. The USD 20 and USD 200 amounts are stated by the authorities that charge them, which the 3 Oct correction did not read. Quotes: Galápagos Governing Council FAQ "Cancelar el pago de la tasa (TCT) $20,00"; Galápagos National Park Directorate (Ordenanza Provincial No. 001-CGREG-30-06-2025) "Turistas extranjeros mayores de 12 años US $200", "menores de 12 años US $100", CAN/Mercosur nationals over 12 "US $100". The cash-only claim stays withdrawn.

entries.old: No separate visa — the Galápagos is part of Ecuador — but there are extra steps. The UK government says you need evidence of a hotel booking or an invitation letter, a return flight to the mainland, a Transit Control Card bought at your departure airport before check-in, and travel health insurance, which is mandatory for foreign tourists. Tourists can stay up to 60 days. The islands' protected areas also charge an entrance fee.
entries.new: No separate visa — the Galápagos is part of Ecuador — but there are extra steps. The UK government says you need evidence of a hotel booking or an invitation letter, a return flight to the mainland, a Transit Control Card bought at your departure airport before check-in, and travel health insurance, which is mandatory for foreign tourists. Tourists can stay up to 60 days a year. The Galápagos Governing Council charges USD 20 for the Transit Control Card, and the Galápagos National Park charges foreign tourists over 12 an entrance fee of USD 200 (USD 100 for citizens of Andean Community and Mercosur countries).
entries.note: Audit: WRONG withdrawal of the USD 20 and USD 200 amounts; both are stated by the charging authorities. Quotes: Galápagos Governing Council FAQ "Cancelar el pago de la tasa (TCT) $20,00"; Galápagos National Park Directorate (Ordenanza Provincial No. 001-CGREG-30-06-2025) "Turistas extranjeros mayores de 12 años US $200", "menores de 12 años US $100", CAN/Mercosur nationals over 12 "US $100". Governing Council FAQ: "hasta cumplir 60 días improrrogables en el año". Bag-screening claim stays withdrawn.

entries.old: Everyone flying to the Galápagos must register at the Galápagos Governing Council desk in Quito or Guayaquil, pay the transit control card fee and have their luggage inspected for biological material before check-in. Keep the card. It is collected when you leave the islands.
entries.new: Everyone flying to the Galápagos needs a Transit Control Card from the Galápagos Governing Council, bought at its counter in Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in, with your ID and a return ticket. It is paid again on every trip. Keep the card: you show it when you enter and when you leave the islands.
entries.note: Consistency: luggage inspection for biological material is not on the cited Governing Council FAQ (and was withdrawn elsewhere on 3 Oct); "collected when you leave" narrowed to the FAQ: "deberá ser presentado tanto al ingreso como a la salida", "por cada viaje realizado deberá cancelar el valor de la Tarjeta".

entries.old: Payable at the Galápagos control desk in Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in; some airlines and tour operators pre-register it.
entries.new: Paid at the Galápagos Governing Council counter in Quito or Guayaquil airport, once per trip. Only travel agencies can buy it in advance, by pre-registering online at least 48 hours before the flight.
entries.note: Consistency: the Governing Council FAQ says advance purchase applies only to travel agencies ("Si lo puede hacer, solo aplica para agencias de viajes. El trámite deberá ser ingresado con 48 horas antes de su vuelo"), not airlines.

entries.old: Both grant the same 30-day stay. The eVisa costs 30 USD, paid online by card; the paper visa on arrival costs 30 USD in cash at the airport counters before immigration, and at Cairo International Airport it is also sold as a QR code by card for 36 USD (including a 6 USD digital service fee). The eVisa avoids the airport queue and is safer if your airline checks visas before boarding. The two lists are not identical: Chinese, Indian and Vietnamese citizens, among others, can use the eVisa but not the visa on arrival, while Jordanian and Lebanese citizens can get the visa on arrival under conditions.
entries.new: Both grant the same 30-day stay. entries.old: Egypt issues a 30-day tourist eVisa through its official portal visa2egypt.gov.eg (30 USD single entry, 65 USD multiple entry) and sells the same visa on arrival for 30 USD cash to a broad list of nationalities, including the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia and Japan; visitors flying directly to the Sinai Red Sea resorts can instead use a free 15-day Sinai-only entry stamp.
entries.new: Egypt issues a 30-day tourist eVisa through its official portal visa2egypt.gov.eg (30 USD single entry, 65 USD multiple entry) and sells the same visa on arrival for 30 USD cash to a broad list of nationalities, including the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia and Japan; visitors who fly into Sharm El-Sheikh and stay under 15 days at the South Sinai resorts of Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba get a free entry stamp instead.
entries.note: Consistency: summary narrowed to the Sinai stamp as the tip and FAQ now give it (arrival by air at Sharm El-Sheikh, under 15 days, four named resorts).

entries.old: El Salvador's security situation has improved dramatically since 2022 — homicide rates are now among the lowest in the Americas and travel advisories have been relaxed accordingly. The state-of-exception security regime remains in force: carry ID, cooperate at checkpoints, and steer clear of anything that could be read as gang imagery, including certain tattoos.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says security has improved considerably with significant reductions in crime, but the risks of violent and petty crime still exist. A state of exception in force since 2022 gives police additional powers, and the police may detain you if they suspect you are a gang member, so always carry identification. Canada says officers at checkpoints may consider tattoos an indication of gang membership.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said homicide rates are 'among the lowest in the Americas' and that advisories 'have been relaxed accordingly', neither stated by the cited UK advice; the FAQ (3 Oct) already uses the UK wording. Rewritten to the UK ('Security in El Salvador has improved considerably with significant reductions in crime. However... the risks of violent and petty crime still exist') and Canada (tattoos at checkpoints).

entries.old: Yes — virtually every nationality needs a visa arranged in advance through an Eritrean embassy; there is no eVisa or visa on arrival. Apply well before your trip: processing regularly takes weeks, approval often depends on referral to Asmara, and it is not guaranteed.
entries.new: Yes — virtually every nationality needs a visa arranged in advance through an Eritrean embassy; there is no eVisa or visa on arrival. Apply well before your trip: the Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says a visa is issued ten working days after it receives the application and fee, and approval is not guaranteed.
entries.note: Consistency: matched the processing-time FAQ and the visa types (10 business days, per the embassy); the "referral to Asmara" claim had no source. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). Tobacco limits depend on the country, and travellers under 17 get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.
entries.new: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). It lists Estonia among the countries applying the lower tobacco limit to all travellers: 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of tobacco. entries.old: The UK Foreign Office says a vehicle not registered in Eswatini needs a customs declaration at the border and a road fund levy of 150 emalangeni (E80 for a motorcycle), payable in South African rand; carry proof of both in the vehicle.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says a vehicle not registered in Eswatini needs a customs declaration at the border and a road fund levy of 150 emalangeni (E80 for a motorcycle), which can be paid in South African rand; carry proof of both in the vehicle.
entries.note: Audit: the FCDO says "These payments can be made with South African Rands" — rand is one way to pay, not the only one; narrowed (the Arabic already said so).

entries.old: Canada advises a high degree of caution because of the risk of civil unrest. Pro-democracy protests have recurred since 2021 and further demonstrations are likely, particularly in Mbabane and Manzini; security forces have used force to disperse crowds, so avoid gatherings. Petty crime, including robbery, is common but lower than elsewhere in southern Africa.
entries.new: Canada advises a high degree of caution because of the risk of civil unrest. Waves of pro-democracy protests took place across the country in 2021 and further demonstrations are likely, particularly in Mbabane and Manzini; security forces have used force to disperse crowds, so avoid gatherings. Petty crime, including robbery, is common but lower than elsewhere in southern Africa.
entries.note: Consistency: Canada says "Waves of pro-democracy protests took place throughout the country in 2021. Further demonstrations are likely"; it does not say they have recurred since.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Vaccination is also widely recommended for travel outside Addis Ababa.
entries.new: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Canada's travel advice says vaccination is recommended depending on your itinerary.
entries.note: Consistency: Vaccination text still said vaccination is 'widely recommended for travel outside Addis Ababa', the claim withdrawn from the FAQ on 3 Oct. Replaced with Canada's wording: 'Vaccination is recommended depending on your itinerary.'

entries.old: Fiji is a relaxed and welcoming destination with little violent crime against visitors, though opportunistic theft from hotel rooms, beaches and rental cars happens and Suva and Nadi warrant normal city caution after dark. The genuine risks are environmental: cyclones between November and April, strong reef currents and rips, and the distance to advanced medical care.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the risk of serious crime is generally low, but there are occasional incidents including sexual assault, and advises care with belongings in cities and popular tourist destinations. It warns of dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries, says cyclones occur throughout the year although the season normally runs from November to April, and notes that healthcare facilities are limited.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text put cyclones 'between November and April' — the claim corrected in bestTimeToVisit on 3 Oct (UK: 'cyclones occur throughout the year') — and described theft from hotel rooms, beaches and rental cars that the cited UK advice does not mention. Rewritten to the UK wording ('The risk of serious crime is generally low, but there are occasional incidents including sexual assault').

entries.old: For Lapland in winter, pack layered thermal clothing, insulated boots and a proper hat.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says winter daylight hours are very short, so you will drive in darkness for most of the day, and icy roads are common and can close roads, particularly in the north. Winter tyres are mandatory from 1 November to 31 March.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. The 3 Oct rewrite still carried packing advice that no official source states. Replaced with Canada's winter statements: 'Daylight hours are very short in the winter, you will need to drive in darkness for most of the day. Icy road conditions are common and may cause road closures, particularly in northern areas.' and 'Winter tires are mandatory between November 1 and March 31.'

entries.old: No official source we checked describes card acceptance in France specifically. The European Central Bank's 2024 payments survey found that across the euro area 89% of in-store transactions were, or could have been, paid without cash, and 95% could be paid in cash.
entries.new: The European Central Bank's 2024 payments survey found that across the euro area 89% of in-store transactions were, or could have been, paid without cash, and 95% could be paid in cash. In France, 9% of consumers said a card or mobile payment had been refused at least once in the previous month, one of the lowest shares in the euro area.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. The euro-area figures are quoted correctly, but 'No official source we checked describes card acceptance in France specifically' is contradicted by the same ECB report, which breaks acceptance down by country: 'at least 10% of consumers had experienced non-acceptance of mobile or card payments ... with the exceptions of the Netherlands (4%), Finland and Estonia (both 8%) and France and Luxembourg (both 9%)'. France's figure added.

The text now opens with the standard 'No official seasonal guidance for visitors.', which keeps the unofficial month list off the page.

entries.old: No official source describes how widely cards are accepted in Guatemala. The UK Foreign Office notes that British pounds often cannot be exchanged and US dollars are much easier, warns of tampered ATMs and says it is safer to change money in hotels, banks or exchange offices. The Government of Canada adds that US dollars can be exchanged at most major banks, and that some ATMs accept foreign debit cards with a four-digit PIN.
entries.new: No official source describes how widely cards are accepted in Guatemala. The UK Foreign Office notes that British pounds often cannot be exchanged and US dollars are much easier, warns of tampered ATMs and says it is safer to change money in hotels, banks or exchange offices. The Government of Canada adds that US dollars can be exchanged at most major banks, and that some ATMs accept Canadian debit cards with a four-digit PIN (five-digit PINs are not accepted).
entries.note: Audit: overreach in the 4 Oct rewrite — Canada says 'Some ATMs will accept Canadian debit cards with a four-digit PIN. Canadian debit cards with a five-digit PIN are not accepted', not foreign cards in general.

entries.old: Violent crime and armed robbery are real concerns, though the main tourist circuit — Antigua, Lake Atitlán, Tikal — is well policed and mostly sees petty theft. Use registered shuttles or app taxis rather than public buses, keep valuables out of sight, and avoid remote roads after dark.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says Guatemala has one of the highest violent crime rates in Latin America, that carjacking and armed robbery are common, and that there have been armed attacks or robberies on most tourist routes between Guatemala City, Antigua, Tikal, Petén and Lake Atitlán. It advises against public buses, recommends radio-dispatched taxis, Uber or hotel taxis for short trips in towns, and advises not travelling alone or at night.
entries.note: Consistency: the old text said the Antigua–Atitlán–Tikal circuit 'is well policed and mostly sees petty theft', contradicting the FCDO (and this page's own FAQ): 'There have been armed attacks or robberies on most tourist routes between Guatemala City, Antigua, Tikal, Petén and Lake Atitlán.' Rewritten to the FCDO's advice.

entries.old: The site that operates Guinea-Bissau's electronic visa application, rgb-visa.com, is currently serving injected advertising links for gambling sites alongside its own content, which is the signature of a compromised web server. We have removed our link to it. Until it is cleaned up, arrange the visa through a Guinea-Bissau embassy or the letter-of-authorisation route for arrival at Bissau airport, and do not enter passport or card details on that site.
entries.new: The site that operates Guinea-Bissau's electronic visa application, rgb-visa.com, is currently serving injected advertising links for gambling sites alongside its own content, which is the signature of a compromised web server. entries.note: Consistency: the tip still offered "the letter-of-authorisation route for arrival at Bissau airport", a visa on arrival that the summary, the FAQ and every row now say no official source confirms. It now points to the embassy route only.

entries.old: Most nationalities do, and it should be arranged before you fly: Guinea-Bissau's embassies (for example in Paris and Lisbon) issue visas in person; Ireland's foreign ministry quotes Irish citizens EUR 70 for 45 days, EUR 110 for 90 days or EUR 200 for 180 days. An eVisa and an airport visa on arrival have been offered, but no official source currently confirms them. Citizens of the 15 ECOWAS countries are exempt and enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol.
entries.new: Most nationalities do, and it should be arranged before you fly: Guinea-Bissau's embassies (for example in Paris and Lisbon) issue visas in person; Ireland's foreign ministry quotes Irish citizens EUR 70 for 45 days, EUR 110 for 90 days or EUR 200 for 180 days. entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from, or having transited more than 4 hours through the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Guyana is itself a yellow fever risk country, so vaccination is strongly recommended for all visitors, and neighboring countries will ask for the certificate when you travel on.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from, or having transited more than 4 hours through the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Guyana is itself on WHO's list of countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.
entries.note: Consistency: the vaccination text still asserted that vaccination is strongly recommended for all visitors and that neighbouring countries ask for the certificate on onward travel — the claims the FAQ correction of 3 October withdrew as unsupported. The WHO list cited states only that Guyana is a risk country; narrowed to that.

entries.old: The UK government's travel advice says visitors can normally stay for 30 days and can apply to Guyana's immigration support services for one-month extensions. Overstaying can lead to arrest, a one-year prison sentence, a fine of up to 50,000 Guyana dollars and deportation at your own expense. Canada's travel advice says to make sure your passport is stamped on arrival.
entries.new: The UK government's travel advice says visitors can normally stay for 30 days. Extensions are granted by Immigration Support Services for three months at a time, at most two. Overstaying can lead to arrest, a one-year prison sentence, a fine of up to 50,000 Guyana dollars and deportation at your own expense. Canada's travel advice says to make sure your passport is stamped on arrival.
entries.note: Consistency: the tip repeated the FCDO's 'one-month extensions', contradicting the stay-extension visa type and the FAQ. Immigration Support Services (the authority, rank 2) states 'Each extension will be a period of three (3) months' and 'A maximum of two (2) Extension of Stay will be granted'; it outranks the FCDO (rank 5).

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says Guyana has two rainy seasons, from May to July and from November to January, but that flooding occurs year round and can hamper overland travel, particularly in coastal areas. No official source we could read names a best time to visit.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Guyana has two rainy seasons, from May to July and from November to January, but that flooding occurs year round and can hamper overland travel, particularly in coastal areas. The months shown are those outside the two rainy seasons; no official source we could read recommends a time to visit.
entries.note: Consistency: the page shows a month list under 'Best time to visit' while the text said no official source names a best time. The text now says what the months are (those outside Canada's two rainy seasons) and that no source recommends a time.

entries.old: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). Tobacco limits depend on the country, and travellers under 17 get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.
entries.new: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). Hungary applies the EU's lower tobacco limit to travellers arriving by land or sea — 40 cigarettes instead of 200 — and travellers under 17 get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.

entries.old: Several Western governments advise against all travel to Iran, citing the risk of arbitrary detention — particularly for dual nationals and journalists — alongside regional conflict. Ordinary crime is low and visitors are generally received warmly, but the political risk is real: check your government's advisory before deciding to go.
entries.new: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments all advise against all travel to Iran, citing the volatile security situation, regional conflict and the risk of arbitrary detention, particularly for dual nationals. The UK government also reports attacks and robberies targeted at foreign nationals and tourists. Check your government's advisory before deciding to go.
entries.note: Consistency: "ordinary crime is low and visitors are received warmly" had no source and contradicts the FCDO ("There have been some attacks and robberies targeted at foreign nationals and tourists"); advisories attributed to FCDO ("advises against all travel to Iran"), Canada ("Avoid all travel") and Smartraveller ("Do not travel").

entries.old: British and Irish citizens travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area. The UK government's travel advice says some airlines and ferry operators require a passport as identification, so check your carrier's rules; other nationalities should carry their passport, and visa-required nationals need an Irish visa even when entering from the UK.
entries.new: British and Irish citizens travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area. The UK government's travel advice says some airlines and ferry operators require a passport as identification, so check your carrier's rules. Other nationalities should carry their passport, and visa-required nationals need an Irish visa even when entering from the UK, unless they qualify under the British Irish Visa Scheme (Chinese and Indian citizens with a UK visa endorsed "BIVS") or Ireland's Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme.
entries.note: Consistency: the tip said every visa-required national needs an Irish visa even when entering from the UK, which contradicts the CN, IN and TR rows (British Irish Visa Scheme; Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme). The exceptions are now named.

entries.old: Common Travel Area: British citizens can live, work and travel in Ireland without any visa or permission, and are not subject to routine passport control arriving from the UK, but airlines still require photo ID, and a passport is the safest document to carry.
entries.new: Common Travel Area: British citizens can live, work and travel in Ireland without any visa or permission. The UK government says a passport is not legally required to enter Ireland, but some airlines and ferry operators require one as identification, so check your carrier's rules.
entries.note: Consistency: aligned with the tip restated on 3 Oct. UK FCDO: "British nationals are not legally required to show a passport to enter Ireland" and "Some airlines and ferry operators have introduced, or will be introducing, a passport-only identification requirement." The unsourced "no routine passport control" and "airlines still require photo ID" were removed.

entries.old: The fee is waived for Jordan Pass holders staying at least 3 nights, and for travelers arriving via Aqaba's special economic zone.
entries.new: The official Jordan Pass site says the fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days); the UK Foreign Office gives the minimum as 3 nights. The fee is also waived for travelers arriving via Aqaba's special economic zone.
entries.note: Consistency: conflict between jordanpass.jo ('stay a minimum of two nights (3 days)', rank 2, the operator) and the FCDO ('stay at least 3 nights', rank 5) resolved by hierarchy; the losing figure is stated beside the winner because this fee cites the FCDO page.

entries.old: Your host — hotel, landlord or inviting organization — must notify the migration authorities of your arrival within 3 working days. Hotels do this automatically; if you stay privately, make sure your host files the notification, as fines can fall on both sides.
entries.new: Your hotel or the person hosting you must register your arrival with the Kazakh authorities within 3 working days of your arrival. If you stay privately, make sure your host does it.
entries.note: Consistency: aligned with the rewritten tip and FAQ; FCDO says "Your hotel or the person hosting you must register your arrival with the Kazakh authorities. They must do this within 3 working days". The unsourced "hotels do this automatically" and "fines can fall on both sides" are dropped.

entries.old: Kazakhstan is generally safe for travelers. Petty crime occurs in cities. Use ride-hailing apps rather than unmarked taxis, and take normal care at night and around bazaars.
entries.new: Kazakhstan is generally safe for travelers. Petty crime occurs in cities. The UK Foreign Office advises against flagging down taxis and recommends licensed, pre-ordered taxi services; take normal care at night and around bazaars.
entries.note: Consistency: the taxi advice now matches the ride-hailing tip and FCDO: "avoid flagging down taxis and use licensed pre-ordered taxi services whenever possible".

Consistency: October was shown as a best month while the text (Canada: "The two rainy seasons usually extend from October to November, and then again from March to mid-June") puts it in the rainy season; October dropped.

entries.old: Bring enough cash for the whole stay. The UK government says very few places accept credit cards and that ATMs are found only at bank branches in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa.
entries.new: Bring enough cash for the whole stay. The UK government says very few places accept credit cards, and that there are ATMs at Bank of Kiribati and ANZ branches in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — the source says "There are ATMs at branches of the Bank of Kiribati and ANZ in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa atoll"; it does not say they are the only ones. Dropped "only".

entries.old: International flights are few, so leave buffer days before any onward international connection.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says severe rainstorms in the November to April rainy season can hamper air and sea travel, so leave buffer days before any onward international connection.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — no official source read (UK FCDO, Canada) says international flights are few. Narrowed to what Canada states: "Severe rainstorms can cause flooding and landslides, which can hamper overland, maritime and air travel."

entries.old: Kosovo is generally safe for visitors, with low street crime and a famously welcoming attitude to travelers. Tensions occasionally flare in the Serb-majority northern municipalities around Mitrovica — follow local advice and avoid protests. In September 2026 large evening gatherings were taking place in Pristina and other towns; allow extra travel time and keep away from crowds.
entries.new: The UK government's travel advice says the political situation is generally stable, but northern Kosovo remains politically sensitive and protests can occur there with little warning; Canada advises against non-essential travel to the northern municipalities of Leposavić, North Mitrovica, Zubin Potok and Zvečan. Pickpockets operate in airports and on public transport. In September 2026 large evening gatherings were taking place in Pristina and other towns; allow extra travel time and keep away from crowds.
entries.note: Consistency: 'low street crime' and 'famously welcoming' had no source (the FCDO warns of pickpockets); the north is now described as the FCDO and Canada advice cited in the tips describe it.

entries.old: Kuwait does not admit Israeli passport holders, and travelers of any nationality whose passports show Israeli stamps or visas are refused entry.
entries.new: Kuwait does not admit Israeli passport holders. The UK government's travel advice says travellers of any nationality whose passports contain an Israeli stamp may be refused a visa or entry.
entries.note: Consistency: the row still said stamped travellers 'are refused entry'; the tip and FAQ were softened on 3 October to the FCDO's 'may be refused a visa or entry'.

entries.old: limited/high: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas. The UK FCDO says ATMs are widely available in the main cities (often with a withdrawal limit around 10,000 KGS), that you should pay in som, and that you should bring cash for rural areas. No official source we could read describes card acceptance.
entries.new: widely/high: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas. The UK FCDO says ATMs are widely available in the main cities (often with a withdrawal limit around 10,000 KGS), that you should pay in som, and that you should bring cash for rural areas. It also says credit and debit cards are widely used around the country: Visa is accepted in most places, though Mastercard is sometimes not, and QR-code payment is common.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the 3 Oct change set "limited" and said no official source describes card acceptance, but the UK FCDO says: "Credit and debit cards are widely used around the country; VISA is accepted in most places, but MasterCard is sometimes not accepted. Payment by QR code is also common." Cash importance stays high (Canada: "The economy is primarily cash-based").

entries.old: (removed)
entries.new: Expect power cuts. The UK says Lebanon's power plants produce only limited electricity for the national grid and that many businesses rely heavily on generators; Canada says power outages and electricity rationing are common, including in Beirut. Keep a torch to hand at night.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the tip was withdrawn as unsupported, but the UK says 'Lebanon's power plants are only producing limited electricity for the national grid. This can lead to power cuts. Many businesses rely heavily on generators', and Canada says 'Power outages and rationing of electricity are common in many parts of the country, including in Beirut.' Restored in sourced form, without the unsourced 'few hours a day' figure.

entries.old: No. Lebanon refuses entry to anyone whose passport or belongings show evidence of travel to Israel — stamps, visas, border-crossing stamps from Jordan or Egypt, or Israeli products. Israeli citizens are barred entirely. If you have visited Israel, travel on a new, clean passport and carry nothing linking you to the trip.
entries.new: Probably not. Canada's travel advice says travel to or from Israel is illegal in Lebanon and that you may be refused entry if your passport bears an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp from a crossing that borders Israel; the UK says an Israeli stamp can lead to refusal even with a valid Lebanese visa. Israeli passport holders are barred entirely.
entries.note: Consistency: the customs note about Israeli products was withdrawn as unsourced; the FAQ now says what the data and Canada state ('You may be refused entry into Lebanon if your passport bears an Israeli visa, an Israeli border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp issued by an office bordering Israel') and matches the Israel row (barred).

entries.old: Lebanon issues free one-month visas on arrival at Beirut airport to citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and many other countries — extendable to three months — while GCC nationals enter visa-free; other nationalities apply through a Lebanese embassy, and any traveler with evidence of travel to Israel is refused entry.
entries.new: Lebanon issues free one-month visas on arrival at Beirut airport to citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and many other countries — extendable to three months — while GCC nationals enter visa-free; other nationalities apply through a Lebanese embassy, and travelers with evidence of travel to Israel may be refused entry.
entries.note: Consistency: both cited governments say travellers with evidence of travel to Israel 'may be refused entry', not that every such traveller is refused.

entries.old: Evidence of travel to Israel leads to refused entry. Canada's travel advice says this includes an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a crossing that borders Israel, and that travel to or from Israel is illegal in Lebanon.
entries.new: Evidence of travel to Israel can lead to refused entry. Canada's travel advice says this includes an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a crossing that borders Israel, and that travel to or from Israel is illegal in Lebanon.
entries.note: Consistency: Canada and the UK say such evidence 'may' lead to refusal.

entries.old: Lebanon and Israel remain formally at war — Israeli passport holders are barred, and any traveler with evidence of travel to Israel is refused entry.
entries.new: Lebanon and Israel remain formally at war — Israeli passport holders are barred, and travelers with evidence of travel to Israel may also be refused entry.
entries.note: Consistency: refusal for evidence of travel to Israel is 'may be refused' in both cited governments' advice.

entries.old: Mar · Apr · May · Sep · Oct · Nov
entries.new: Mar · Apr · May · Sep · Oct
entries.note: Consistency: the months shown included November, which the text (and Canada: 'Violent thunderstorms occur in the summer (November to February) and result in several deaths yearly') places in the storm season. The months are now only those outside both windows Canada names (June–August snow, November–February storms).

entries.old: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Lesotho. Canada's travel advice says to expect extreme cold and heavy snowfall in the mountains from June to August, which can close roads and passes, and violent thunderstorms from November to February.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says to expect extreme cold and heavy snowfall in the mountains from June to August, which can close roads and passes, and violent thunderstorms from November to February. The months shown are those outside both periods; no official source we could read recommends a time to visit.
entries.note: Consistency: the page shows a month list under 'Best time to visit' while the text opened by saying no official source gives a best time. The text now says what the months are (those outside Canada's snow and thunderstorm periods) and that no source recommends a time.

entries.old: (removed)
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says power and water outages are common in Liberia, there is no landline telephone service and mobile phone communication may be disrupted — plan accordingly.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — the 3–4 Oct withdrawal said no official source supports the tip, but Smartraveller states "Power and water outages are common. There's no landline telephone service in Liberia, and mobile phone communication may be disrupted." Restored that part only; the plug/voltage wording stays out (IEC source currently unreadable).

entries.old: Yes. US passport holders must obtain a visa before travel from a Liberian embassy or consulate; fees for US applicants are set on a reciprocity basis. There is no visa on arrival for tourists.
entries.new: Yes. US passport holders must obtain a visa before travel from a Liberian embassy or consulate. The Consulate General in New York charges US citizens USD 180 for a three-year multiple-entry visa. Liberia's online e-visa, issued at Roberts International Airport, is for applicants with no Liberian embassy in their country.
entries.note: Consistency: "fees set on a reciprocity basis" is not stated; the fee data gives USD 180 for US citizens (three-year multiple entry). "No visa on arrival" contradicted the e-visa type, which is issued at Roberts International Airport but only where there is no Liberian embassy in the applicant's country.

entries.old: No — tourists cannot rely on a visa on arrival. Arrange your visa before travel through an embassy or Liberia's eVisa channel; airlines will normally refuse boarding without one.
entries.new: Only with approval in advance. Liberia Immigration Service's online e-visa (USD 102.50, non-refundable) is approved before travel and the visa is then issued at Roberts International Airport only; apply at least 7 days before your flight. If there is a Liberian embassy in your country, you must apply there instead.
entries.note: Consistency: the FAQ said tourists cannot get a visa on arrival and that airlines refuse boarding (unsourced); the e-visa data says the visa is approved online, issued at Roberts International Airport only, USD 102.50, apply at least 7 days ahead, and applicants with a Liberian embassy in their country must apply there.

entries.old: Liberia is stable but poor, with opportunistic street crime in Monrovia. Avoid displaying valuables, use trusted drivers after dark, and remember that emergency services and medical care are minimal.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says Liberia is generally stable politically but the crime rate is high, mostly opportunistic theft; foreigners have been mugged in Monrovia's Mamba Point and Sinkor areas. It advises not carrying valuables in public, not walking around Monrovia or isolated areas after dark, and arranging transport in advance. There is no reliable ambulance service.
entries.note: Consistency: "stable but poor" and "use trusted drivers" are not stated by the cited FCDO advice; rewritten to it ("Liberia is generally stable politically"; "The crime rate in Liberia is high"; "There is no reliable ambulance service in Liberia").

entries.old: No sponsor, no visa: a tourist visa application on Libya's eVisa portal must be sponsored by a tourism company registered with the Passports, Nationality and Foreigners Affairs Authority, and must include the company's letter naming the tour group and destination. The small number of operators running escorted tours handle this for you.
entries.new: No sponsor, no visa: a tourist visa application on Libya's eVisa portal must be sponsored by a tourism company registered with the Passports, Nationality and Foreigners Affairs Authority, and must include the company's letter naming the tour group and destination.
entries.note: Consistency: 'The small number of operators running escorted tours handle this for you' repeats the escorted-tour claim withdrawn from the tourism FAQ on 3 October as unsourced.

entries.old: Liechtenstein applies Schengen rules through its association agreement: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180-day period, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa — issued on Liechtenstein's behalf by Swiss missions, since the principality has no airport and is entered via Switzerland or Austria.
entries.new: Liechtenstein applies Schengen rules through its association agreement: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180-day period, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa — issued on Liechtenstein's behalf by Swiss missions, since the principality has no international airport and is entered via Switzerland or Austria.
entries.note: Consistency: Summary said Liechtenstein has 'no airport'; the tip was narrowed on 3 Oct to Canada's wording: 'There is no international airport.'

entries.old: Liechtenstein is one of the safest countries in the world, with negligible crime. The only practical hazards are alpine ones. Check conditions before mountain hikes.
entries.new: The UK government says crime levels are low, but there are instances of petty street crime such as bag-snatching and pickpocketing. It also warns of alpine hazards, including a risk of avalanches in mountainous areas all year round, so check conditions before mountain hikes.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said crime is 'negligible' and that the only hazards are alpine; the cited UK advice says 'Crime levels are low, but there are instances of petty street crime.' Rewritten to the source.

entries.old: Luxembourg is one of Europe's safest countries. Petty theft around the capital's train station district is the main, minor concern. Keep an eye on bags there late at night.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says violent crime is not common in Luxembourg's cities, though violent robberies have happened. Pickpockets operate on buses and in train stations, particularly the main station, Gare de Luxembourg, and hotel lobbies in the Findel area are reported to be hotspots for theft.
entries.note: Consistency: the cited FCDO page says "Violent crime is not common in Luxembourg cities. However, violent robberies have happened" and "Pickpockets operate on buses and in train stations, particularly in the main train station, Gare de Luxembourg. Hotel lobbies in the Findel area are reported to be hotspots"; it does not call Luxembourg one of Europe's safest countries or call theft a minor concern. Arabic mirrored.
