entries.note: Audit: the European Commission page says only that EU policy "ensures that water intended for human consumption can be consumed safely", which describes the Directive's aim and says nothing about Luxembourg. The Luxembourg government states the fact itself: "L'eau du robinet au Luxembourg est en fait l'un des aliments les plus réglementés, contrôlés et sûrs, disponibles." gouvernement.lu is now on the allowed list. Value unchanged (true); the source moved to the destination government (rank 3).

entries.old: (removed on 3 Oct: "The duty-free tobacco allowance is only 19 cigarettes — excess quantities are fined heavily.")
entries.new: Macao Customs lets each passenger bring in, without declaring it, up to 19 cigarettes, 1 cigar (of no more than 3 g) and 25 g of leaf tobacco, and 1 litre of drinks over 30% alcohol; declare anything beyond these quantities.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct withdrawal was wrong — Macao Customs' table of goods for personal use (Chief Executive Dispatches 209/2021 and 208/2022) lists "19 unidades de cigarros", "1 unidade de charutos (o peso dos charutos não pode exceder, por unidade, 3 gramas)", "25 gramas das folhas de tabaco" and "As bebidas de 1 litro com teor alcoólico que exceda 30%". Restored from that table; the unsourced "fined heavily" was not.

entries.old: (removed on 3 Oct: "E-cigarettes and vaping products may not be brought into Macao. They are prohibited items.")
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says it is prohibited to import, export or distribute e-cigarettes, vaporizers and their refills in Macao, and that offenders can expect heavy fines.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct withdrawal was wrong — Canada's travel advice for Macao: "It is prohibited to import, export and distribute e-cigarettes, vaporizers and their refills. Convicted offenders can expect heavy fines." Restored and attributed.

entries.old: No government publishes seasonal guidance for visitors. The UK FCDO says the cyclone season normally runs from November to April and that many secondary roads are impassable except by 4-wheel-drive in the December–April rainy season.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives seasonal guidance for visitors. The UK FCDO says the cyclone season normally runs from November to April and that many secondary roads are impassable except by 4-wheel-drive in the December–April rainy season.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — we can only say no official source we read gives seasonal guidance, not that no government publishes any. The FCDO figures (cyclones November–April, rainy season December–April) are confirmed: "The cyclone season in Madagascar normally runs from November to April."

entries.old: Yes, but it is easy: every nationality can obtain a tourist visa, either on arrival at the airport or online in advance at evisamada.gov.mg. Visas come in 15-, 30- and 60-day versions, with the fee depending on length of stay.
entries.new: Yes, but it is easy: every nationality can obtain a tourist visa, either on arrival at the airport or online in advance at evisamada-mg.com. Visas come in 15-, 30- and 60-day versions, with the fee depending on length of stay.
entries.note: Consistency: the FAQ named evisamada.gov.mg, but the visa types apply at evisamada-mg.com, the portal the data cites.

entries.old: Both lead to the same tourist visa. Applying at evisamada.gov.mg before travel saves queueing after a long flight, while the visa on arrival remains available to all nationalities at international airports — if you choose it, carry the fee in cash.
entries.new: Both lead to the same tourist visa. Applying at evisamada-mg.com before travel saves queueing after a long flight, while the visa on arrival remains available to all nationalities at international airports — if you choose it, carry the fee in cash.
entries.note: Consistency: the FAQ named evisamada.gov.mg, but the visa types apply at evisamada-mg.com, the portal the data cites.

entries.old: Most visits are trouble-free, but political conditions have been volatile since the change of government in late 2025, and robbery and petty crime are risks in Antananarivo and on isolated beaches. Avoid demonstrations, do not walk in cities after dark, and use trusted drivers for long road journeys.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says robberies and thefts are commonplace throughout Madagascar and that there have been violent robberies and assaults on isolated beaches, even in daytime. It advises avoiding political demonstrations and large gatherings, not walking alone in city centres or poorly lit areas after dark, and using pre-booked taxis or hotel transport.
entries.note: Consistency: "most visits are trouble-free" and "use trusted drivers" are not stated by the cited FCDO page; rewritten to what it says ("Robberies and thefts are commonplace throughout Madagascar"; "do not walk alone in city centres or poorly lit urban areas after dark").

entries.new: FCDO EUR 7,500 (published) vs Canada EUR 10,000 (conflict)
entries.note: Consistency: Canada (updated 26 May 2026) says "you must declare your foreign currency in excess of 10,000 euros"; the FCDO (updated 9 September 2026) says "Declare foreign cash or travellers cheques if the value is 7,500 euros or more". Same rank; the newer FCDO page wins (newer), Canada recorded as the conflict.
Consistency: March was shown as a best month while the text gives Canada's rainy (monsoon) season as November to March; March dropped.

entries.old: ["The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in anything deemed contrary to Islam, including idols for worship, bibles, pork and pork products, and alcohol.", "Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export tortoise shell and coral."]
entries.new: ["The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in anything deemed contrary to Islam, including idols for worship, bibles, pork and pork products, and alcohol.", "Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export tortoise shell and coral.", "Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to import pornography, alcohol or pork products, though alcohol and pork may be consumed on resort islands."]
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the 3 Oct entry withdrew the pornography import ban as having no official source, but Smartraveller states: "It's illegal to import pornography, alcohol or pork products; however, alcohol and pork may be consumed on resort islands." (read from https://web.archive.org/web/20260526085932/https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/asia/maldives; live page refuses with an HTTP/2 error). Restored as attributed. The drone-declaration and airport-storage withdrawals stand.

entries.new: AU: 911 for all services (resolved: newer)
entries.note: Consistency: two sources disagree. UK FCDO getting-help (updated 12 Aug 2026): 'Ambulance: 102 Fire: 118 Police: 119', matching Canada (26 May 2026: police 119, medical 102, firefighters 118). Smartraveller (snapshot 26 May 2026, page updated 20 January 2026): 'General emergency Call 911' for every service. Same rank; the newer page wins (newer); Smartraveller recorded in source.conflict. Numbers unchanged.

entries.old: Crime is low on the resort islands, but petty theft happens — do not leave things unattended on the beach or in unlocked rooms. Outside the resorts there is gang-related violence, including knife crime, mainly in Malé and Hulhumalé; avoid empty roads on foot after dark. Strong tidal currents cause drownings, so swim only in supervised or designated areas.
entries.new: Crime is low on the resort islands, but petty theft happens — do not leave things unattended on the beach or in unlocked rooms. Outside the resorts there is gang-related violence, including knife crime, mainly in Malé and Hulhumalé; avoid empty roads on foot after dark. Strong tidal currents can drag swimmers away from the shore and cause drownings, so ask resort staff where it is safe to swim.
entries.note: Consistency: the FCDO says strong tidal currents 'can drag you away from the shoreline resulting in drownings' and to 'speak to the appropriate resort staff to find out where it is safe for you to swim'; it does not mention supervised or designated areas.

entries.old: Your passport (or travel document) must be machine-readable and valid for at least 1 month on arrival — though at least 6 months is recommended, as some airlines apply the stricter standard.
entries.new: Your passport (or travel document) must be machine-readable and valid for at least 1 month on arrival, according to Maldives Immigration; the UK Foreign Office gives the same 1-month rule. Canada's travel advice asks for 6 months from your date of entry, so check with your airline.
entries.note: Consistency: 'at least 6 months is recommended, as some airlines apply the stricter standard' had no source. FCDO: 'expiry date at least one month after the date you arrive'. Canada: 'valid for at least 6 months from your date of entry' — recorded in source.conflict; Maldives Immigration (the authority, rank 2) outranks Canada (hierarchy).

entries.old: No official source we could read gives seasonal travel guidance for Mali.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice describes three seasons: dry and cool from November to February, dry and hot from March to June, when temperatures can reach 45°C, and rainy from June to October, when seasonal flooding can hamper overland travel. Both Canada and the UK advise against all travel to Mali.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the withdrawal said no official source gives seasonal guidance, but Canada's advice names three seasons: 'the dry and cool season, from November to February; the dry and hot season, from March to June, where temperatures can reach 45°C; the rainy season, from June to October'. The UK FCDO also gives the rainy season as June to October. The months already shown (Nov–Feb) are Canada's dry and cool season.

entries.old: No official source we could find states whether travel insurance is required to enter the Marshall Islands. Majuro Hospital and the Ebeye clinic provide basic care only and serious cases are flown to Honolulu or Guam, so cover with air evacuation is worth having.
entries.new: No official source we could find states whether travel insurance is required to enter the Marshall Islands. The UK government says medical facilities are very limited and advises comprehensive travel insurance covering all medical costs, including medical evacuation.
entries.note: Consistency: the Majuro Hospital / Ebeye clinic / flights to Honolulu or Guam detail was withdrawn from tips[medical-limits] as unsourced but was still asserted here. Now what the FCDO says: 'Medical facilities are very limited. Make sure you have comprehensive travel insurance which covers all medical costs, including medical evacuation.'

entries.old: Visitors must show a confirmed onward or return ticket and where they will stay. With the island-hopper and Nauru Airlines services running only a few times a week, immigration expects a realistic departure date.
entries.new: Visitors must show a confirmed onward or return ticket and where they will stay.
entries.note: Consistency: the sentence about island-hopper and Nauru Airlines frequencies was withdrawn from tips[flight-connections] as unsourced but was still asserted here; removed.

entries.old: The west-coast corridor (Nouakchott, Nouadhibou, Banc d'Arguin) and the western Adrar around Atar, Chinguetti and Ouadane see travelers routinely. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to the east and to within 25 km of the Mali border because of terrorism risk, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the interior, including the southern provinces. Petty crime is moderate; the bigger constraints are distance, heat and thin infrastructure.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to the east and to within 25 km of the Mali border because of terrorism risk, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the interior, including the southern provinces. It says crime levels are moderate but steadily increasing, with thefts and robberies at knifepoint on unlit, isolated beaches in Nouakchott.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text still said the west-coast corridor and western Adrar 'see travelers routinely' — the 'growing tourist circuit' claim withdrawn from the FAQ on 3 Oct — and called petty crime 'moderate' with unsourced remarks on distance and heat. Rewritten to the UK advice: 'Crime levels are moderate but steadily increasing.'

entries.old: Rest of the world rate (USD 60); nationals of the Arab world and Africa pay EUR 40 (USD 45). Paid in cash (euros or US dollars) on arrival after applying online. Bring the exact amount, as change and receipts are rarely given.
entries.new: Rest of the world rate (USD 60); nationals of the Arab world and Africa pay EUR 40 (USD 45). Paid in cash (euros or US dollars) on arrival after applying online. Bring the exact amount: the UK government says change and receipts are not given.
entries.note: Consistency: Fee note said change and receipts are 'rarely given'; the tip (and the UK source: 'Change and receipts are not given') say they are not given.

entries.old: No official source we could read describes card acceptance in Mauritius.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says you can use credit cards at most hotels, restaurants and large shops, and that there are ATMs in most towns and in large shopping centres; it advises checking with your bank that your cards will work in Mauritius.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the 3 October entry said no official source describes card use, but Smartraveller (read live 4 October) states: 'You can use credit cards at most hotels, restaurants and large shops.' and 'There are ATMs in most towns and in large shopping centres.'

entries.old: (removed)
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says travellers aged 18 or over can bring into Mexico up to 20 packs of cigarettes, 25 cigars or 200 grams of tobacco, 3 litres of alcoholic beverages and 6 litres of wine; bringing more means a hefty import tax, even if you declare it.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the allowance note was withdrawn as unsupported, but Canada's travel advice states it: 'If you're 18 or older, you can bring into Mexico up to: 20 packs of cigarettes; 25 cigars or 200 grams of tobacco; 3 litres of alcoholic beverages; 6 litres of wine.' Restored, attributed.

entries.old: Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to carry firearms or ammunition without a permit, including in Mexican waters; apply for a permit at a Mexican embassy or consulate before you arrive.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to carry firearms or ammunition without a permit, including in Mexican waters; apply for a permit at a Mexican embassy or consulate before you arrive. Canada's travel advice says anyone entering Mexico with a firearm or ammunition without prior written authorization from the Mexican authorities is subject to imprisonment.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the rewrite dropped the arrest risk as unsourced, but Canada's travel advice says 'Anyone entering Mexico with a firearm or ammunition without prior written authorization from Mexican authorities is subject to imprisonment.' Added, attributed; the unsourced 'single forgotten cartridge' wording stays out.

There is no online system. Keep the departure portion in your passport until you leave."}

entries.note: Consistency: the cited FCDO page says only 'If you do not hold a valid entry permit you must complete “Customs, Immigration & Quarantine Form (CIQ Form)” on arrival'. The inbound-flight hand-out, the separate departure portion and 'no online system' are not stated there and were dropped.

entries.old: widely-in-cities/medium — The UK FCDO says paying by card is now generally widespread, though not always possible, particularly outside Chișinău; US dollars and euros are the most widely accepted foreign currencies, and notes should be in perfect condition. Foreign cards do not work at banks in Transnistria, which uses its own Transnistrian ruble.
entries.new: limited/high — The Government of Canada says credit cards are increasingly accepted but the economy is primarily cash-based, and that only a few ATMs in Chișinău accept foreign bank cards. The UK FCDO says US dollars and euros are the most widely accepted foreign currencies and that notes should be in perfect condition. Foreign cards do not work in Transnistria, which uses its own Transnistrian ruble.
entries.note: Consistency: the payments text (FCDO, updated 10 Dec 2025: 'Paying by card is now generally widespread') contradicted tips[cash-lei] (Canada, last updated 26 May 2026: 'Credit cards are increasingly being accepted, but the economy is primarily cash-based', 'only a few accept foreign bank cards'). Same rank (foreign travel advice); the newer page wins. FCDO recorded in source.conflict; its non-conflicting currency and note-condition advice kept, attributed.

entries.old: Most visitors need Myanmar's official tourist eVisa — 28 days, US$50, open to roughly 100 nationalities and valid only for arrival at the main international airports or the Kawthaung land border — while most ASEAN passport holders enter visa-free for short stays (Malaysians need the eVisa). Ongoing civil conflict keeps most land borders closed to foreigners and large parts of the country off-limits.
entries.new: Most visitors need Myanmar's official tourist eVisa — 28 days, US$50, open to roughly 100 nationalities and valid only for arrival at the main international airports or the Kawthaung land border — while most ASEAN passport holders enter visa-free for short stays (Malaysians need the eVisa). Canada says land crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of neighbouring states, and the UK advises against all travel to much of the country.
entries.note: Consistency: Summary still said land borders are 'closed to foreigners', the claim withdrawn from the tip and FAQ on 3 Oct; aligned with what Canada and the UK say.

entries.old: Myanmar is in a state of armed conflict following the 2021 military coup — most governments advise against all travel, or against all nonessential travel. Fighting, airstrikes and arbitrary detention occur across much of the country, and areas under martial law are closed to foreigners.
entries.new: Myanmar is in armed conflict following the 2021 military coup. Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar, and the UK advises against all travel to much of the country. Canada reports regime airstrikes and drone strikes causing civilian casualties; the UK says some areas are under martial law or curfews, and both warn of a risk of arbitrary detention.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said 'most governments' advise against travel and that martial-law areas are 'closed to foreigners' — the latter is the claim withdrawn from the tips on 3 Oct. Rewritten to what Canada and the UK state (UK: 'Some areas in Myanmar are under martial law; others have curfews'; Canada: 'you are at risk of arbitrary detention').

entries.old: ASEAN visa exemption — up to 14 days visa-free arriving at the international airports; land borders are largely closed, so confirm conditions before travel.
entries.new: ASEAN visa exemption — up to 14 days visa-free arriving at the international airports. Canada says land border crossings may close with little or no notice, so confirm conditions before travel.
entries.note: Consistency: Row note said land borders are 'largely closed', the claim withdrawn on 3 Oct; aligned with Canada ('Border crossings may close with little or no notice').

entries.old: Namibia keeps visa-free entry for SADC citizens and reciprocating states, but since April 1, 2025 it requires a visa from other nationalities — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada and Japan, which can get it on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals); nationalities not on the visa-on-arrival list must obtain an e-visa before travel.
entries.new: Namibia keeps visa-free entry for most SADC citizens and for reciprocating states, but since April 1, 2025 it requires a visa from other nationalities — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada and Japan, which can get it on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals); nationalities not on the visa-on-arrival list must obtain an e-visa before travel.
entries.note: Consistency: the rows for three SADC members — DR Congo (evisa), Comoros and Madagascar (visa-on-arrival) — are not visa-free, so the summary now says "most SADC citizens".

entries.old: It changed in 2025. SADC citizens and nationals of countries that waive visas for Namibians still enter visa-free. Since April 1, 2025, citizens of many previously-exempt countries — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Japan — must obtain a visa, available on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 per adult (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals). Nationalities not on the visa-on-arrival list must get an e-visa before travelling.
entries.new: It changed in 2025. Most SADC citizens and nationals of countries that waive visas for Namibians still enter visa-free. Since April 1, 2025, citizens of many previously-exempt countries — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Japan — must obtain a visa, available on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 per adult (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals). Nationalities not on the visa-on-arrival list must get an e-visa before travelling.
entries.note: Consistency: DR Congo, Comoros and Madagascar, all SADC members, need a visa per their rows; "SADC citizens" became "Most SADC citizens".

entries.old: Citizens of SADC countries (South Africa, Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Angola and the rest) and of states that reciprocate Namibia's waiver — for example Russia, Singapore and Malaysia — continue to enter without a visa, typically for up to 90 days. Confirm your status before travel as the lists are periodically reviewed.
entries.new: Citizens of most SADC countries (South Africa, Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Angola and others, but not DR Congo, Comoros or Madagascar) and of states that reciprocate Namibia's waiver — for example Russia, Singapore and Malaysia — continue to enter without a visa, typically for up to 90 days. Confirm your status before travel as the lists are periodically reviewed.
entries.note: Consistency: "SADC countries (... and the rest)" contradicted the CD (evisa), KM and MG (visa-on-arrival) rows; the three exceptions are now named.

entries.new: (none)

No official source names them, so the months are cleared rather than shown as a recommendation.

entries.new: This nationality cannot apply on arrival.

entries.old: A visitor's visa can be granted for up to three months, single entry (Immigration Regulations 2014, regulation 12(7)), and the fee rises with the length: AUD 50 for one month, 150 for two and 250 for three. In practice the flight schedule sets the length of most visits. Extensions are possible through the immigration office on the island but should not be assumed.
entries.new: A visitor's visa can be granted for up to three months, single entry (Immigration Regulations 2014, regulation 12(7)), and the fee rises with the length: AUD 50 for one month, 150 for two and 250 for three. Extensions are possible through the immigration office on the island but should not be assumed.
entries.note: Consistency: the flight-frequency claim was withdrawn from tips[flights] as unsourced on 3 Oct but this FAQ still relied on it; sentence removed.

Consistency: the page headed the text with these months as the best time to visit, but the text says there is 'No official seasonal guidance for visitors' and cites only the FCDO's monsoon warning ('normally June to October'). No official source names them, so the months are cleared rather than shown as a recommendation.

entries.old: Payable at the border in major currencies (cash preferred; card terminals at Kathmandu airport are unreliable). You can pre-fill the online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np within 15 days before arrival to skip the kiosk line.
entries.new: Payable at the border. The UK FCDO says you can pay by card but should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars the preferred currency. You can pre-fill the online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np within 15 days before arrival to skip the kiosk line.
entries.note: Consistency: the claim that Kathmandu airport card terminals are unreliable was withdrawn from tips[voa-cash] because it contradicts the FCDO ('You can pay by card, but you should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars being the preferred currency') but was still asserted in the fee notes.

entries.old: Payable at the border in major currencies (cash preferred; card terminals at Kathmandu airport are unreliable). You can pre-fill the online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np within 15 days before arrival to skip the kiosk line.
entries.new: Payable at the border. The UK FCDO says you can pay by card but should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars the preferred currency. You can pre-fill the online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np within 15 days before arrival to skip the kiosk line.
entries.note: Consistency: the claim that Kathmandu airport card terminals are unreliable was withdrawn from tips[voa-cash] because it contradicts the FCDO ('You can pay by card, but you should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars being the preferred currency') but was still asserted in the fee notes.

entries.old: Payable at the border in major currencies (cash preferred; card terminals at Kathmandu airport are unreliable). You can pre-fill the online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np within 15 days before arrival to skip the kiosk line.
entries.new: Payable at the border. The UK FCDO says you can pay by card but should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars the preferred currency. You can pre-fill the online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np within 15 days before arrival to skip the kiosk line.
entries.note: Consistency: the claim that Kathmandu airport card terminals are unreliable was withdrawn from tips[voa-cash] because it contradicts the FCDO ('You can pay by card, but you should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars being the preferred currency') but was still asserted in the fee notes.

entries.old: Yes, but it is issued on arrival: US passport holders (like almost all nationalities) get a tourist visa at Kathmandu airport or any land border — 30 USD for 15 days, 50 USD for 30 days or 125 USD for 90 days, multiple entry. Bring the fee in cash.
entries.new: Yes, but it is issued on arrival: US passport holders (like almost all nationalities) get a tourist visa at Kathmandu airport or any land border — 30 USD for 15 days, 50 USD for 30 days or 125 USD for 90 days, multiple entry. You can pay by card, but bring cash as a back-up; US dollars are preferred.
entries.note: Consistency: 'Bring the fee in cash' implied cash only; the FCDO says you can pay by card, with cash (US dollars preferred) as a back-up, as tips[voa-cash] now says.

entries.old: On arrival you complete a form (or bring the receipt from the free online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np, submitted within 15 days before travel), pay the fee in cash and receive the visa sticker. Queues at Kathmandu airport can be long — the pre-filled form and exact cash speed things up.
entries.new: On arrival you complete a form (or bring the receipt from the free online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np, submitted within 15 days before travel), pay the fee (by card, or in cash — the UK FCDO advises carrying US dollars as a back-up) and receive the visa sticker. Queues at Kathmandu airport can be long — the pre-filled form speeds things up.
entries.note: Consistency: said the fee is paid in cash; the FCDO says 'You can pay by card, but you should have cash as a back-up', as tips[voa-cash] now says.

entries.old: Border officers may ask to see a travel insurance document covering healthcare costs, repatriation and other emergencies in Nepal, along with confirmation of where you will spend your first night. Nepal's Department of Immigration does not list insurance among its visa-on-arrival steps (online form, fee receipt, passport), so this rests on the UK government's advice. For trekking, choose a policy that covers your maximum altitude and helicopter evacuation: a rescue flight can cost thousands of dollars.
entries.new: Border officers may ask to see a travel insurance document covering healthcare costs, repatriation and other emergencies in Nepal, along with confirmation of where you will spend your first night. Nepal's Department of Immigration does not list insurance among its visa-on-arrival steps (online form, fee receipt, passport), so this rests on the UK government's advice. For trekking, the UK FCDO advises insurance that covers mountain rescue and helicopter costs; it says helicopter evacuation usually costs between £1,000 and £2,000 or more per flying hour.
entries.note: Consistency: the 'maximum altitude' policy advice was withdrawn from tips[altitude-insurance] as unsourced; now the FCDO's wording: 'Make sure your insurance includes cover for mountain rescue services and helicopter costs' and evacuation by helicopter 'usually costs between £1,000 and £2,000 or more per flying hour'.

entries.old: The Netherlands is a very safe destination. The main visitor risks are pickpocketing in central Amsterdam and on trains, and bicycle theft.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common, particularly in central Amsterdam and around Amsterdam Central Station, and that thieves work in gangs on trains and trams to and from Schiphol airport. Amsterdam police have also warned of criminals posing as police to trick tourists into handing over cash and cards.
entries.note: Consistency: "a very safe destination" and "bicycle theft" are not stated by the cited FCDO advice; rewritten to it ("Pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common, particularly in central Amsterdam and around Amsterdam Central Station").

entries.old: Declare all food and any outdoor gear when you arrive. The UK says it is illegal to import most food products, that tents, fishing equipment and golf clubs can carry pests, and that breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.
entries.new: Declare any food or outdoor gear that may be prohibited, and if in doubt, declare it. The UK says it is illegal to import most food products, that tents, fishing equipment and golf clubs can carry pests, and that breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.
entries.note: Consistency: aligned with the customs notes — the UK says to declare 'anything that may be prohibited' and, 'if in doubt', to declare items to Biosecurity New Zealand; it does not say all food and all gear must be declared.

entries.old: Check the latest security advisories: most of Niger is rated do-not-travel.
entries.new: Check the latest security advisories: the UK and Canadian governments advise against all travel to Niger.
entries.note: Consistency: row notes said 'most of Niger' is do-not-travel while countryFacts.safety and the tips say the UK advises against all travel to the whole country (FCDO: 'FCDO advises against all travel to Niger'; Canada: 'Avoid all travel to Niger').

entries.old: A return or onward ticket is part of the e-Visa application and is checked by airlines before boarding.
entries.new: The Nigeria Immigration Service lists evidence of a return ticket among the requirements for a tourism visa.
entries.note: Consistency: the NIS page says only 'Evidence of return ticket.' among the visa requirements; 'checked by airlines before boarding' is not stated (the same airline-check claim was withdrawn from the landing-card FAQ on 3 Oct).

entries.old: Not a condition of entry, but strongly recommended — private healthcare in Lagos and Abuja is decent but expensive, and serious cases may need evacuation.
entries.new: Not a condition of entry. Canada's travel advice says public and private medical facilities usually require a cash deposit, a payment guarantee or confirmation of medical insurance, that you will likely need medical evacuation in case of serious illness or injury, and recommends travel insurance that covers evacuation and hospital stays.
entries.note: Consistency: the cited NIS visa page does not mention insurance or healthcare; 'private healthcare in Lagos and Abuja is decent' had no source. Rewritten to Canada: 'Public and private medical facilities usually require an initial cash deposit, a payment guarantee, or a confirmation that you have medical insurance... You will likely need medical evacuation'. Source changed to Canada.

entries.old: Most travelers do. Since May 2025 short tourist and business visits are handled through Nigeria's official e-Visa, open to more than 180 nationalities including the US, UK, Canada and the EU. ECOWAS citizens enter without a visa under the bloc's free-movement protocol, as do citizens of Cameroon and Chad under visa-abolition agreements, and a small number of nationalities must still apply at a Nigerian embassy.
entries.new: Most travelers do. Since May 2025 short tourist and business visits are handled through Nigeria's official e-Visa, open to more than 180 nationalities including the US, UK, Canada and the EU. ECOWAS citizens enter without a visa under the bloc's free-movement protocol, as do citizens of Cameroon and Chad under visa-abolition agreements.
entries.note: Consistency: 'a small number of nationalities must still apply at a Nigerian embassy' contradicts the visa policy, where every one of the 182 non-exempt passports is e-Visa-eligible and none is embassy-only; clause removed.

entries.old: Risk varies sharply by state. Lagos, Abuja and much of the south-west are visited routinely with sensible precautions, but the FCDO advises against all travel to Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, Katsina and Zamfara states and to the riverine areas of the Niger Delta, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the north, the Middle Belt and parts of the south-east, because of terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. Plan state by state against current advisories.
entries.new: Risk varies sharply by state. The FCDO advises against all travel to Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, Katsina and Zamfara states and to the riverine areas of the Niger Delta, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the north, the Middle Belt and parts of the south-east, because of terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. Plan state by state against current advisories.
entries.note: Consistency: removed 'Lagos, Abuja and much of the south-west are visited routinely with sensible precautions', which the FCDO does not state; the state list matches the FCDO page.

entries.old: Cash only. The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted, that the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies with Chinese yuan taken in some places, and that importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice adds that there are no ATMs.
entries.new: Mostly cash. The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted, that the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies with Chinese yuan taken in some places, and that importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice says cash is the most accepted form of payment and there are no ATMs, though some hotels accept credit cards if you give them advance notice.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — 'Cash only' contradicts Canada's 'Some hotels accept credit cards if you give them advance notice' (the payments text already says so); 'Cash is the most accepted form of payment.'

entries.old: North Korea is essentially closed to tourism: borders shut in 2020 and have reopened only for limited, state-organized group tours aimed chiefly at the Russian market. Tourists normally travel only on organised tours whose state-approved operator arranges the visa, independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and US and South Korean passport holders cannot visit at all.
entries.new: North Korea is essentially closed to tourism: the UK government says its borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and only limited tourism has restarted. Tourists normally travel only on organised tours whose state-approved operator arranges the visa, independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and US and South Korean passport holders cannot visit at all.
entries.note: Consistency: the 'Russian market' group-tour claim was withdrawn from the tips and FAQ on 3 October as unsourced; the summary now states the UK's position.

entries.old: Yes — every visitor needs a visa, and it can only be arranged through a state-approved tour operator as part of an organized, guided tour. In practice tourism has been essentially closed since 2020, with only limited group tours (mainly for the Russian market) resuming. US and South Korean passport holders cannot visit at all.
entries.new: Yes — every visitor needs a visa. The UK government says tourists can normally travel only as part of an organised tour, and independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs. It also says the borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and only limited tourism has restarted. US and South Korean passport holders cannot visit at all.
entries.note: Consistency: 'only through a state-approved tour operator' contradicted the independent-travel FAQ (sponsor and MFA permission), and the 'mainly for the Russian market' claim was withdrawn elsewhere as unsourced.

entries.old: Limited Russian group tours resumed in 2024. The visa is arranged by the tour operator through the DPRK embassy as part of the package.
entries.new: All visitors need a visa arranged through a state-approved tour operator as part of an organized tour; tourism has been essentially closed since 2020 and applications are accepted only when tours are running.
entries.note: Consistency: 'Limited Russian group tours resumed in 2024' has no official source and was withdrawn from the tips and FAQ on 3 October; the row now carries the general note.

entries.old: Most Western governments advise against all travel to North Korea, citing the serious risk of arbitrary arrest and long-term detention. US passports cannot be used for travel there at all under US law.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea, and Canada advises against all travel, citing the risk of arbitrary detention. US passports cannot be used for travel there at all under US law.
entries.note: Consistency: 'Most Western governments advise against all travel' contradicted the safety text (the UK advises against all but essential travel); now names the two governments' advice as published.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says the rainy season runs from late June until August, with July usually the wettest month.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the rainy season runs from late June until August, with July usually the wettest month. No official source names a best season; the months shown fall outside the rainy season.
entries.note: Consistency: the months shown (April, May, September, October) are not an official recommendation; the text now says so, as on other destinations.

entries.old: Foreign visitors must be registered with the police within 48 hours of arrival. Hotels and registered guesthouses do this automatically; if you stay privately, your host must register you at the local police station. Unregistered stays can cause fines or problems on departure.
entries.new: You must register with the local police in the town or city where you are staying within 48 hours of arrival. Hotel staff register you at check-in; otherwise register with the police directly (also possible online, in Macedonian) and de-register 24 hours before you leave. Keep the registration document until you leave: failing to register can bring a fine, detention and a court hearing, or a restriction on returning.
entries.note: Consistency: Declaration text said 'your host must register you' and that unregistered stays cause 'problems on departure', neither of which the cited UK page says; rewritten to the UK wording ('If you're staying in a hotel, staff will register you at check-in... If you have registered with the police directly, you must de-register 24 hours before you leave'). Canada's 24-hour figure, now named in the tip, is recorded as the losing side of a conflict (same rank; UK page updated 13 Aug 2026, Canada 26 May 2026 → newer).

entries.old: (none)
entries.new: Canada: within 24 hours (resolvedBy newer)
entries.note: Consistency: The tip names Canada's 24 hours beside the UK's 48; the declaration published 48 with no record of the disagreement. Recorded Canada as the losing source: same rank, the UK page is newer (13 Aug 2026 vs 26 May 2026).

entries.old: North Macedonia is generally safe, with little crime affecting tourists beyond occasional pickpocketing in Skopje. Drive defensively — road conditions and driving standards vary outside the main highways.
entries.new: The UK government says attacks against foreign nationals are extremely rare, but gangs of children pickpocket and bag-snatch in the main shopping and entertainment areas late at night, and there are occasional shooting incidents, including in Skopje, not targeted at foreign nationals. Canada says secondary roads are poorly maintained and lack adequate lighting.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said there is 'little crime affecting tourists beyond occasional pickpocketing in Skopje'; the cited UK advice also reports shooting incidents and gang pickpocketing in which 'Foreign nationals appear to have been specifically targeted'. Rewritten to the UK wording; the road remark attributed to Canada.

entries.old: Norway is in the Schengen Area through its association agreement with the EU: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities including the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa — while remote Svalbard is visa-free for all nationalities.
entries.new: Norway is in the Schengen Area through its association agreement with the EU: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities including the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa Svalbard, though Norwegian, is outside the Schengen Area.
entries.note: Consistency: the Svalbard tip and FAQ withdrew 'visa-free for all nationalities' (no official source we could read); the summary now says only what Canada's advice states, that Svalbard is outside Schengen.

entries.old: The main cities and northern tourist circuits (Hunza, Skardu) generally receive visitors warmly, but several governments advise against travel to areas near the Afghan border, parts of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa because of terrorism risk. Check current advisories, stick to open areas and confirm whether your route needs a No Objection Certificate.
entries.new: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Balochistan, to within 10 miles of the Afghan border and to many districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and against all but essential travel to Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and says there is an ongoing risk of terrorism. Check current advisories, and ask the local authorities whether your route needs a No Objection Certificate.
entries.note: Consistency: said governments advise against "parts of Balochistan", contradicting the FAQ and the FCDO ("FCDO advises against all travel to Balochistan Province"); unsourced claim about Hunza and Skardu removed; rewritten to the FCDO areas list.

entries.new: (none)
entries.note: Consistency: the months shown as best (November to April) include April and November, which the text's FCDO source puts in the higher-rainfall period ('higher rainfall from April to November'), and the text says there is no official seasonal guidance. Months cleared.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says you must sign the Palau Pledge, which is stamped in your passport on arrival, and complete the Palau entry form within 72 hours of arriving.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says you must sign the Palau Pledge, which is stamped in your passport on arrival. Submit the Palau Entry Form online in the 72 hours before you depart; it generates a QR code to show at check-in and on arrival.
entries.note: Consistency: the tip said to complete the entry form 'within 72 hours of arriving' (FCDO wording, readable as after arrival), while entryRequirements.declarations[arrival-declaration], from the Palau government portal, says it is submitted online at most 72 hours before departure and shown at check-in. Tip aligned with the declaration.

entries.old: Crime is a genuine concern, especially in Port Moresby and Lae, where carjacking, robbery and opportunistic street crime occur. Most visitors travel with pre-arranged transfers, avoid walking after dark, and stay clear of highlands areas affected by tribal violence. Rural and resort areas are generally calmer.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says there is a high risk of serious crime in Port Moresby, Lae and Mount Hagen, that carjacking and other vehicle crime are common, and that walking after dark is particularly dangerous in urban centres. It advises against all but essential travel to Hela and Southern Highlands provinces and to Enga (except Wabag District) because of tribal fighting.
entries.note: Consistency: 'most visitors travel with pre-arranged transfers' and 'rural and resort areas are generally calmer' had no source; restated as the FCDO advice the FAQ already cites.

entries.old: The Government of Canada says Paraguay has extreme dry periods between April and September and a rainy season from December to March, when the east is most exposed to flooding and roads, especially in the Chaco, can become impassable. Bush and forest fires are common from mid-July to December in the north-east (Concepción, Amambay, San Pedro, Canindeyú).
entries.new: No official seasonal guidance. The Government of Canada says Paraguay has extreme dry periods between April and September and a rainy season from December to March, when the east is most exposed to flooding and roads, especially in the Chaco, can become impassable. Bush and forest fires are common from mid-July to December in the north-east (Concepción, Amambay, San Pedro, Canindeyú).
entries.note: Consistency: Canada describes hazards ("Paraguay experiences extreme dry periods between April and September"; fires "common between mid-July to December"), not a best season, yet the page showed May–September as the best time. Text now says no official seasonal guidance exists, which hides the month list.

entries.old: police 105 · medical 116 · fire 116
entries.new: police 105 · ambulance 106 · fire 116
