Same rank, so the newer page wins (newer) — that is the FCDO, not Canada; Canada is now the recorded conflict.

entries.old: Buy Machu Picchu entry tickets and Inca Trail permits well in advance, through official channels only.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. Neither the FCDO nor Canada says to buy Machu Picchu tickets or Inca Trail permits in advance or through official channels; the FCDO's Inca trail section covers only medical services and safety. Tip withdrawn.

entries.old: The UK government says altitude sickness is a serious risk in parts of Peru, including Cusco, Puno, the Colca Canyon and Kuelap. Plan a light first day, stay hydrated and learn the symptoms.
entries.new: The UK government says altitude sickness is a serious risk in parts of Peru, including Cusco, Puno, the Colca Canyon and Kuelap. Canada's travel advice says the risk starts at 2,500 metres and is higher if you ascend quickly or exercise or drink alcohol before you get used to the altitude.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. FCDO: 'Altitude sickness is a serious risk in parts of Peru, including Cusco, Puno, the Colca Canyon and Kuelap.' confirmed; the added advice was unsourced and is replaced by Canada's: 'You're at risk of high-altitude illnesses if you travel 2,500 metres above sea level or more … more at risk if you ascend quickly; exercise or drink alcohol before you get used to the altitude.'

entries.old: Most visits to Peru's tourist circuit are trouble-free, but petty theft is common in Lima and Cusco, express kidnappings via unofficial taxis occur, and some border and remote coca-growing regions (the VRAEM) should be avoided. Use registered taxis or ride-hailing apps and keep valuables out of sight.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says street crime, including muggings and thefts, is a significant problem in Lima, Cusco, Arequipa and other major cities; that tourists, especially those travelling alone, are at risk of 'express kidnapping', often by criminals posing as taxi drivers; and that the border areas with Ecuador, Colombia and Brazil and the VRAEM carry a higher risk because of organised crime linked to drug production. It advises licensed telephone or app-based taxis rather than hailing one on the street.
entries.note: Consistency: 'most visits are trouble-free' is not stated by the cited FCDO page; rewritten to what it says ('Street crime, including muggings and thefts, is a significant problem in Lima, Cusco, Arequipa and other major cities').

entries.old: … Amazonas (Iquitos, Puerto Maldonado, Tambopata) …
entries.new: … Amazonas (Iquitos, Puerto Maldonado, Tarapoto) …
entries.note: Consistency: aligned the FAQ's example towns with the yellow-fever entry requirement text (MINSA lists the regions Loreto, Madre de Dios, San Martín, Ucayali and Amazonas).

entries.old: ["The UK government says there are strict rules on goods taken into or out of the Philippines, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty."]
entries.new: ["The UK government says there are strict rules on goods taken into or out of the Philippines, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.", "The Bureau of Customs says all arriving passengers fill in the electronic Customs Baggage Declaration Form (e-CBDF) on the eTravel website or the eGovPH app within 72 hours before arrival, and those carrying currency above the allowed threshold also fill in the electronic Currencies Declaration Form (e-CDF); the eTravel QR code is shown to the customs officer for clearance."]
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct entry withdrew the eTravel customs-declaration claim as unconfirmed, but the Bureau of Customs (already cited on currency limits) states it: "all arriving and departing passengers can now fill-out the electronic Customs Baggage Declaration Form (e-CBDF) and electronic Currencies Declaration Form (e-CDF), as applicable, using the e-Travel website"; "The e-CBDF must be filled-out by all arriving passengers". Restored, attributed. The duty-free allowance withdrawal stands.

entries.old: Book an onward or return ticket before you fly: the UK government says most visitors are expected to have proof of return or onward travel and that immigration officials and airlines may ask for it.
entries.new: Book an onward or return ticket before you fly: the Department of Foreign Affairs says visa-free visitors must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination, and the UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for it.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct rewrite said "most visitors"; the FCDO says "Most UK visitors are also expected to have proof of return or onward travel". The rule itself is the DFA's: visa-free nationals "must also possess return tickets to their country of origin or outward-bound tickets to their next country of destination".

entries.old: Plan on it. The UK government says most visitors are expected to have proof of return or onward travel and that immigration officials and airlines may ask for it, and Canada says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.
entries.new: Yes, for visa-free visitors. The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for it, and Canada says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.
entries.note: Consistency: the FAQ said "Plan on it" while entryRequirements.onwardTicket is required for visa-free arrivals; the DFA states visa-free nationals "must also possess return tickets ... or outward-bound tickets". Also narrowed the FCDO attribution ("Most UK visitors").

entries.old: Visa-free entry legally requires an onward or return ticket, and airlines enforce this strictly at check-in — travelers without one are routinely denied boarding.
entries.new: The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for proof of it.
entries.note: Consistency: "airlines enforce this strictly ... routinely denied boarding" had no source (withdrawn from the FAQ on 3 Oct); kept the requirement the DFA states.

entries.old: The Philippines admits citizens of more than 150 countries visa-free for 30 days — extendable by 29 days at a Bureau of Immigration office — and requires every arriving traveler to register on the free eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival. Airlines strictly check onward tickets before boarding.
entries.new: The Philippines admits citizens of more than 150 countries visa-free for 30 days — extendable by 29 days at a Bureau of Immigration office — and requires every arriving traveler to register on the free eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival. Visa-free visitors must also hold a return or onward ticket.
entries.note: Consistency: "Airlines strictly check onward tickets before boarding" had no source; replaced with the DFA requirement.

entries.old: Poland is one of Europe's safest destinations, with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing on public transport in Warsaw and Kraków and avoid unlicensed taxis.
entries.new: The UK government says most visitors do not experience any difficulties and serious crime against foreigners is rare, though some attacks have been racially motivated. It warns that criminals view foreigners as easy targets for street crime and petty theft in crowded and tourist areas, at main rail stations and on trains, and that passengers have been attacked in unofficial taxis and ride-share cars.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text called Poland 'one of Europe's safest destinations' and placed pickpocketing in Warsaw and Kraków, neither stated by the cited UK advice, and said only to avoid unlicensed taxis, while the licensed-taxis tip (3 Oct) notes attacks in ride-share cars too. Rewritten to the UK wording ('Serious crime against foreigners is rare, but crimes do occur and in some cases attacks have been racially motivated').

entries.old: (removed)
entries.new: The EU's Your Europe portal says that when you arrive from outside the EU you can bring in, free of VAT and excise duty and not for resale, 200 cigarettes (or 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco), 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits over 22% or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine, and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 if you travel by air or sea). Travellers under 17 get no tobacco or alcohol allowance.
entries.note: Audit: the 4 Oct withdrawal was wrong — the EU's Your Europe page states the allowance: '200 cigarettes or 100 cigarillos or 50 cigars or 250 g tobacco' (higher limit; Portugal is not among the lower-limit countries), '1 litre of spirits over 22 % vol.' and 'other goods up to a value of €300 per traveller or €430 for travellers by air and sea'. Restored in the page's own terms.

entries.old: Portugal consistently ranks among the safest countries in the world. The main visitor risk is pickpocketing in Lisbon and Porto, especially on trams and at viewpoints.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office advises being alert to street crime: take care on public transport and at crowded bus and tram stops, where thieves use distraction techniques and often work in teams. Attacks, including sexual assaults, are rare but do occur, most often late at night around nightlife areas.
entries.note: Consistency: 'consistently ranks among the safest countries in the world' is not in the cited FCDO advice; rewritten to its words: 'Be alert to the risk of street crime. Take care on public transport and at crowded bus and tram stops. Thieves use distraction techniques and often work in teams' and 'Attacks including sexual assaults, are rare but do occur.'

entries.old: {"tapWaterSafe": true, "source": {"url": "https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/water/drinking-water_en", "name": "European Commission — Drinking water", "type": "igo", "lastVerified": "2026-10-04"}}
entries.new: null (no source)
entries.note: Audit: the European Commission page says only that EU policy "ensures that water intended for human consumption can be consumed safely". That is the Drinking Water Directive's aim, and it says nothing about Portugal. No Portugal-specific official source we read (FCDO, Canada, Smartraveller) states that tap water is safe, so the value is withdrawn to null.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says Qatar has zero tolerance for drug offences, even residual amounts, and that some medicines legal elsewhere are controlled or illegal in Qatar. To bring controlled or prescription medication, follow the Ministry of Public Health's steps, including a prescription and a medical report in English; the Ministry runs an online permit service.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says Qatar has zero tolerance for drug offences, even residual amounts, and that some medicines legal elsewhere are controlled or illegal in Qatar. To bring controlled or prescription medication, follow the Ministry of Public Health's steps, including carrying a prescription and a medical report in English or Arabic, issued within the last 6 months; the Ministry runs an online permit service.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the FCDO says 'carrying a prescription and medical report in English or Arabic containing details of your medication and treatment, issued within the last 6 months'; the 3 October text said 'in English' only and dropped the 6-month condition.

entries.old: {"url": "https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/congo-brazzaville", "name": "Government of Canada — Republic of the Congo travel advice and advisories", "type": "government", "lastVerified": "2026-10-04"}
entries.new: {"url": "https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/congo-brazzaville", "name": "Government of Canada — Republic of the Congo travel advice and advisories (last updated 8 September 2026)", "type": "government", "lastVerified": "2026-10-04", "lastChanged": "2026-10-04", "conflict": {"url": "https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/congo/getting-help", "name": "UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Republic of Congo travel advice: getting help (updated 2 June 2026)", "states": "There's no central number for emergency services; report crimes to local police on 06 665 4804", "resolvedBy": "newer"}}
entries.note: Consistency: Canada (last updated 8 September 2026) lists "police: 117, firefighters: 118"; the FCDO getting-help page (updated 2 June 2026) says "There's no central number for emergency services ... You can report crimes to local police on 06 665 4804". Same rank; the newer Canada page wins (numbers unchanged) and the FCDO statement is recorded in source.conflict.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate (and, in some cases, a polio certificate) to pass border control. Keep it with your passport.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says you must have certificates proving yellow fever and polio vaccination to pass border control. Keep it with your passport.
entries.note: Consistency: the vaccinations data marks polio requiredWhen "always", and the FCDO says "To pass border control ... you must have certificates to prove you've had: a yellow fever vaccination ... a polio vaccine"; "in some cases" removed. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: Not for most travelers. Rwandan ordinary-passport holders get a free visa on arrival for up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement; for everyone else there is no reliable visa on arrival for tourists. Arrange your visa through a Congolese embassy before traveling; airlines will normally refuse boarding without one.
entries.new: Not for most travelers. Rwandan ordinary-passport holders get a free visa on arrival for up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement; for everyone else, Canada's travel advice says a visa cannot be obtained at ports of entry, or at any Congolese embassy other than the one for your country of residence. Arrange your visa there before traveling.
entries.note: Consistency: matched the row notes and Canada ("You cannot obtain a visa at ports of entry or at any Embassy of the Republic of the Congo other than the one of your country of residence"); the airline-boarding claim had no source. Arabic mirrored.

entries.old: (removed)
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says to use only licensed metered taxis that display their price lists, not to hail a taxi on the street but to order one from your hotel or use a trusted ride-sharing app, and at Bucharest's Henri Coandă airport to take a taxi from the booth in the arrivals terminal to get a fair rate.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the 3 Oct removal said no official page supports it, but Canada's advice says: "Use only licensed metered taxis that display their price lists... At the Bucharest Henri Coandă International Airport, arrange for a taxi from the taxis booth within the arrivals terminal to get a fair rate. Don't hail a taxi on the street; instead, order one from your hotel or use a trusted ride-sharing app." Restored as what Canada says; the unsourced Gara de Nord claim stays out.

entries.old: Romania is one of the EU's safer destinations with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing on public transport in Bucharest, taxi overcharging around stations and the airport, and stray dogs in some areas. Drones from the war in neighboring Ukraine have crossed into Romanian airspace and some carrying explosives have landed or washed ashore: follow RO-Alert warnings and do not approach military debris.
entries.new: Romania is one of the EU's safer destinations with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing on public transport in Bucharest, unlicensed taxis (Canada's travel advice says not to hail one on the street), and stray dogs in some areas. Drones from the war in neighboring Ukraine have crossed into Romanian airspace and some carrying explosives have landed or washed ashore: follow RO-Alert warnings and do not approach military debris.
entries.note: Consistency: "taxi overcharging around stations and the airport" is not what the cited advice says; Canada says "Don't hail a taxi on the street" and to use licensed metered taxis. Aligned with the restored taxi tip.

entries.old: Russia issues a unified 30-day eVisa to citizens of some 60 countries including most of the EU, admits CIS neighbors and much of Latin America and the Gulf visa-free, and requires an embassy visa from US, UK, Canadian and Australian travelers. Note that most Western governments currently advise against all travel to Russia.
entries.new: Russia issues a unified 30-day eVisa to citizens of some 60 countries including most of the EU, admits CIS neighbors and much of Latin America and the Gulf visa-free, and requires an embassy visa from US, UK, Canadian and Australian travelers. Note that the UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Russia and Canada says to avoid all travel.
entries.note: Consistency: attributed like the rewritten travel-advisories tip and safe-now FAQ. FCDO: "FCDO advises against all travel to Russia"; Canada (travel.gc.ca/destinations/russia): "Avoid all travel to Russia". The broader "most Western governments" was not checked against an official page.

entries.old: Most Western governments currently advise against all travel to Russia because of the war in Ukraine, drone attacks, limited flights and consular help, and the risk of arbitrary detention — with dual nationals facing exit bans and mobilisation rules. Everyday street crime is low away from border regions, but the overall situation warrants treating travel as high-risk.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Russia and Canada says to avoid all travel. The FCDO cites drone attacks and air-defence activity, a lack of flights, very limited consular support, an increased risk of detention and a high likelihood of terrorist attacks, including in major cities. It says British-Russian dual nationals are treated as Russian citizens, and that people whose draft notice appears on the electronic register cannot leave Russia.
entries.note: Consistency: brought into line with the safe-now FAQ, which dropped the unsourced street-crime claim; "most Western governments" replaced by the two governments actually read. FCDO: "Russian law prevents eligible individuals from leaving Russia once their draft notice appears on the federal electronic draft register"; "If you hold both British and Russian nationality, Russian authorities will treat you as a Russian citizen."

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says the last Saturday of each month is Umuganda, a national day of community service, when most normal services close from 7 am to 11 am.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the last Saturday of each month is Umuganda, a national day of community service, when most normal services close from 7 am to 11 am.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG attribution. Canada's Rwanda page does not mention Umuganda; the wording is the FCDO's: "The last Saturday of each month is Umuganda, a national day of community service. Most normal services close from 7am to 11am."

entries.old: Yes — visitor visas can be extended through the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration (applications go through the Irembo portal) before your current stay expires. Apply a week or more ahead and be ready to show onward plans and means of support.
entries.new: Some visa classes can be extended. Rwanda's Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration says the details are set out in the information for applicants for each visa class; apply before your current stay expires.
entries.note: Consistency: narrowed to what the immigration directorate says ("Some visa classes may be extended. Details are set out in the Information for applicants for each class."); the "a week or more ahead" and onward-plans/means-of-support advice had no source.

entries.old: The hurricane season runs from June to November, according to the UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada. Take insurance that covers storm cancellation and be ready to change plans at short notice.
entries.new: The hurricane season runs from June to November, according to the UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada. Canada says even small tropical storms can quickly develop into major hurricanes during this period, and to weigh the risks carefully when planning a trip in that season.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. The 3 Oct trim kept unsourced insurance advice. Canada: 'During this period, even small tropical storms can quickly develop into major hurricanes … You should carefully consider these risks when planning a trip during the hurricane season.'

entries.old: … Check schedules locally and do not plan tight same-day connections to a flight.
entries.new: St Kitts and Nevis are separate islands; the Government of Canada says ferry services run between them and to Antigua and Barbuda and Montserrat.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. Canada states only 'Ferry services are available between Saint Kitts and Nevis, Antigua and Barbuda, and Montserrat.'; the scheduling advice was unsourced and is removed.

entries.old: eta · 90 days, extendable 90 · 'Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days.'
entries.new: eta · 180 days · 'The UK Foreign Office says British citizens can visit without a visa for up to 6 months; to stay longer, apply and pay for an extension through the Immigration Department.'
entries.note: Consistency: FCDO entry requirements: 'You can visit St Kitts and Nevis without a visa for up to 6 months.' The row's default source (MFA visa-required list) states no stay length, so the explicit statement wins; the unsourced 90-day extension figure is dropped.

entries.old: Saint Lucia is straightforward for visitors, with the main risks being opportunistic theft, break-ins at unattended villas and yachts, and persistent hustling around Castries and the beaches. Violent crime is concentrated in specific districts away from the resorts.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says to take normal security precautions in Saint Lucia. It reports that violent crime, including gun violence, has increased over the past year, particularly in Vieux Fort, and that petty crime such as pickpocketing and purse snatching rises around festivals, carnival and the winter holiday season.
entries.note: Consistency: the old text ('violent crime is concentrated in specific districts away from the resorts') is not what the cited source says; Canada: 'Violent crime, including gun violence, has increased over the past year, particularly in Vieux Fort.' Rewritten to the source, attributed.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Saint Lucia. Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November.
entries.note: Consistency: the page shows the months beside this text as a best time; the source states only the hurricane season, so the text now says no official source gives a best time (as on other destinations).

entries.old: Samoa is calm and welcoming, with low levels of violent crime. The usual issues are petty theft from open fales and vehicles, strong ocean currents and reef cuts, and driving hazards — narrow roads, roaming dogs and pigs, and driving on the left since 2009.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says the level of serious crime is low and petty theft is uncommon and opportunistic. Tides can produce powerful currents in lagoons and waves break directly onto reefs, so take local advice before swimming or surfing. Stray dogs are common in Apia and many villages, and roads are poorly lit at night.
entries.note: Consistency: the text still asserted "driving on the left since 2009", which was withdrawn from the drive-left tip on 3–4 Oct as unconfirmed; rewritten to the FCDO ("The level of serious crime is low, and incidents of petty theft are uncommon and opportunistic"; "Stray dogs are common in Apia and in many villages").

entries.old: The free 90-day entry permit is granted on the condition that you hold a confirmed onward or return ticket; airlines check this before boarding.
entries.new: The free 90-day entry permit is granted only if you have a return or onward ticket, a passport valid at least 6 months after you leave Samoa, and a visa or permit for the country you travel on to.
entries.note: Consistency: "airlines check this before boarding" is not stated by Samoa Immigration; it lists the conditions: "Have a return or onward ticket … Have a valid visa or permit for entry into the country to which they will travel from Samoa."

entries.old: Yes. The free permit is conditional on holding a confirmed onward or return ticket, and airlines check it at check-in. You should also be able to name accommodation for at least the first part of your stay.
entries.new: Yes. Samoa Immigration grants the free visitor permit only if you have a return or onward ticket. You must also state your accommodation arrangements — a hotel or resort, or the village and family name if staying with family or friends.
entries.note: Consistency: removed "airlines check it at check-in" (not stated by Samoa Immigration); accommodation condition quoted from it: "State their accommodation arrangements … (specifically the village and family name)".

entries.old: San Marino has no airport and no border controls of its own — you enter through Italy, so Schengen rules decide everything: EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-waiver nationals walk straight in, while other travelers need an Italian Schengen visa.
entries.new: San Marino has no border controls of its own — you must travel through Italy to enter, so Schengen rules decide everything: EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-waiver nationals walk straight in, while other travelers need an Italian Schengen visa.
entries.note: Consistency: "no airport" was withdrawn with the getting-there tip and FAQ as unsourced; the FCDO states only "You will need to travel through Italy to enter San Marino" and "You do not need to pass through border controls to enter San Marino".

entries.old: San Marino is one of Europe's safest destinations — even petty theft is rare, including at the height of the tourist season. Normal precautions are enough.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says street crime is very rare, but you should still take precautions to keep your passport and money safe; Canada describes the crime rate as low.
entries.note: Consistency: "one of Europe's safest" and "even at the height of the tourist season" are not stated by an official source; rewritten to FCDO ("Street crime is very rare, but you should take precautions to keep your passport and money safe") and Canada ("The crime rate is low").

entries.old: {"general": "117"}
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the 3 October conflict was decided by recency on the premise that Canada's page dated from December 2025, but it reads 'Last updated: 25 June 2026', newer than the FCDO's getting-help page ('Updated: 19 June 2026'). Same rank, newer page wins: Canada's 'police: 112, medical assistance: 999, firefighters: 033 / 300 / 301' is published and the FCDO's '117 (ambulance, fire, police)' recorded as the conflict.

entries.old: Sierra Leone has been peaceful since 2002 and visitors are generally welcomed warmly. The main risks are petty theft in Freetown, road accidents and occasional political demonstrations. Avoid crowds, and take care on the roads at night.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the political situation has improved since the civil war ended in 2002 but can change, and protests can turn violent, so avoid political gatherings and follow any curfews. It reports robberies of British nationals, sometimes at knifepoint, in parts of Freetown and at peninsula beach resorts, and advises completing road journeys in daylight. Canada says armed robberies, carjackings and burglaries have occurred in foreigners' homes, with a higher risk of serious crime after dark.
entries.note: Consistency: 'peaceful since 2002 and visitors are generally welcomed warmly ... main risks are petty theft' is the verdict withdrawn from the safety FAQ on 3 October as unsourced; the FCDO and Canada describe armed robbery and violent crime.

entries.old: The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned: it is illegal to bring them into Singapore, including for personal use, and those found with them have them confiscated and could be fined. | Australia's Smartraveller says you may not bring in any chewing gum, including nicotine gum, even if you stay within the airport transit zone. | Australia's Smartraveller says penalties for drug offences include caning and the mandatory death sentence for some trafficking offences.
entries.new: The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned: it is illegal to bring them into Singapore, including for personal use, and those found with them have them confiscated and could be fined. | Singapore Customs says there is no duty-free concession for cigarettes and tobacco products: all of them, including packs bought in Singapore with the duty-paid (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST when brought in, and packs that do not meet Singapore's standardised-packaging rules are disposed of at the checkpoint. | Australia's Smartraveller says you may not bring in any chewing gum, including nicotine gum, even if you stay within the airport transit zone. | Australia's Smartraveller says penalties for drug offences include caning and the mandatory death sentence for some trafficking offences.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the 'no duty-free allowance for cigarettes' note was removed as unsupported, but Singapore Customs states it: "There is no duty-free concession or GST import relief for cigarettes and tobacco products. All cigarettes and tobacco products, including those purchased in Singapore with the Singapore Duty-Paid Cigarette (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST when brought into Singapore." Restored, attributed to Singapore Customs.

entries.old: (removed)
entries.new: Singapore Customs says there is no duty-free allowance for cigarettes or tobacco: every pack you bring in, even one bought in Singapore with the duty-paid (SDPC) mark, is subject to duty and GST, so declare it on arrival.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the cigarette tip was removed as having no official source, but Singapore Customs states: "There is no duty-free concession or GST import relief for cigarettes and tobacco products. All cigarettes and tobacco products, including those purchased in Singapore with the Singapore Duty-Paid Cigarette (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST when brought into Singapore." Restored, attributed; the unsourced 'heavy fines' claim is not restored.

entries.old: Vapes and e-cigarettes: no — the UK government says they are banned and illegal to bring in, even for personal use. Cigarettes: you must declare anything that may be subject to tax or duty; we could not confirm Singapore's tobacco allowance from an official source.
entries.new: Vapes and e-cigarettes: no — the UK government says they are banned and illegal to bring in, even for personal use. Cigarettes: yes, but Singapore Customs says there is no duty-free allowance for them — all cigarettes and tobacco products, even packs bought in Singapore with the duty-paid (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST, so declare them on arrival.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG — the FAQ said no official source confirms Singapore's tobacco allowance; Singapore Customs states: "There is no duty-free concession or GST import relief for cigarettes and tobacco products. All cigarettes and tobacco products, including those purchased in Singapore with the Singapore Duty-Paid Cigarette (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST when brought into Singapore."

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season runs from December to March (northeast monsoon) and from June to September (southwest monsoon).
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season runs from December to March in the northeast and from June to September in the southeast.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH — Canada's advice says "The rainy (or monsoon) season extends from: December to March in the northeast; June to September in the southeast"; it names regions, not a 'southwest monsoon'. Restated in the source's words.

entries.old: Driving on Slovak motorways requires a vignette, sold online at eznamka.sk and at border crossings, petrol stations and post offices. The UK government says you could get a heavy fine without one.
entries.new: Driving on Slovak motorways requires a vignette. The toll operator's site eznamka.sk is the only official sales channel online, and its points of sale are mostly at selected petrol stations and at border crossings. The UK government says you could get a heavy fine without one.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. Neither eznamka.sk nor the FCDO sells vignettes at post offices: eznamka.sk calls itself "The only official sales channel for Slovak motorway vignettes" and says points of sale are "located most often at selected petrol stations within the Slovak Republic and at border crossings"; the post offices it lists are user-support points for record changes. FCDO: "You can get a motorway vignette at all major border crossings into Slovakia and at larger petrol stations."

entries.old: Slovakia is a safe, low-crime country. Petty theft can occur around Bratislava's main station and busy tourist spots; in the High Tatras, respect weather warnings and stay on marked trails.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says there is a risk of petty crime, especially in Bratislava, where pickpockets operate around the main tourist areas, the Christmas markets and bars. If hiking, it advises staying on marked trails and checking local warnings before setting out.
entries.note: Consistency: the "main station" hotspot and "low-crime" description had no source. FCDO: "There is a risk of petty crime, especially in Bratislava... Pickpockets operate around the main tourist areas, particularly the Christmas markets and in bars"; "If hiking, stay on marked trails... and check local warnings before setting out."

entries.old: Cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when entering or leaving the EU. There are no controls at internal Schengen borders.
entries.new: Cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when entering or leaving the EU. Canada's travel advice says this does not apply when travelling within the EU.
entries.note: Consistency: 'There are no controls at internal Schengen borders' contradicted the FAQs and the UK advice ('Allow extra time for crossing Slovenia's land borders and be ready to show your passport'). Replaced with Canada's statement that the declaration 'does not apply if you are travelling within the European Union'.

entries.old: police: 999 · ambulance: 111 · fire: 988 (conflict with Canada resolved by "hierarchy")
entries.new: police: 999 · ambulance: 111 · fire: 988 (Smartraveller; Canada's 911 kept in source.conflict, resolved by "newer")
entries.note: Audit: the earlier "hierarchy" resolution was wrong, since FCDO, Canada and Australia are all foreign travel advice of the same rank. The newest of the three, Smartraveller (updated 28 September 2026), says "Fire and rescue services Call 988. Medical emergencies Call 111 or go to the hospital. Police Call 999", which agrees with FCDO ("Ambulance: 111", 26 May 2026). Canada (16 September 2026, "Medical emergencies: 911") is the loser, resolvedBy newer. The Smartraveller text sits in collapsed sections and has to be read from the page's full textContent.

entries.old: Virtually every government advises against all travel to Somalia due to terrorism, armed conflict, crime and a very high kidnapping risk. Al-Shabaab regularly attacks hotels, government sites and the airport road in Mogadishu, and visitors move with pre-arranged armed security. Somaliland is calmer: the UK advises against all but essential travel to its Awdal, Maroodijeh (Hargeisa) and Sahil regions, and against all travel to the rest of Somalia, including the rest of Somaliland.
entries.new: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except the Awdal, Maroodijeh and Sahil regions, where it advises against all but essential travel; Canada advises avoiding all travel. The FCDO says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks, including on hotels and Mogadishu International Airport, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping throughout the country, including Somaliland.
entries.note: Consistency: the armed-escort claim withdrawn from the do-not-travel tip was still asserted here, and "virtually every government" is not what the sources say. Rewritten to FCDO ("Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Somalia, including Somaliland"; "There is a high threat of kidnapping throughout Somalia") and Canada ("Avoid all travel to Somalia").

entries.old: (removed on 3 Oct: "Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes, 2 bottles of alcohol (up to 2 liters total, under 400 USD) and goods worth up to 800 USD per adult.")
entries.new: The Korea Customs Service's duty-free allowance is goods worth up to USD 800 in total, plus, on top of that, alcohol of up to 2 litres and USD 400, 200 cigarettes, 20 ml of e-cigarette liquid nicotine and 100 ml of perfume; travellers under 19 get no allowance for alcohol or cigarettes.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct withdrawal was wrong — the Korea Customs Service's passenger guide states "US$800 or less of the total taxable value of goods" and "Apart from the section above (total volume up to 2L and US$400), 200 cigarette sticks, e-cigarette/liquid nicotine 20ml ... and 100ml of perfume"; "Minors under 19 years of age ... are not given tax exemption for liquor and cigarettes." Restored from that page (it gives no bottle count).

entries.old: (none)
entries.new: The Korea Customs Service says meat, plants, fruit, vegetables and other agricultural, livestock and fishery products, including processed foods, must be declared on arrival. Goods over the allowance that are found undeclared carry an extra 40% on top of the duty.
entries.note: Audit: the withdrawn note ("cannot be brought in") overstated the rule, but the KCS guide does list "Animal (including meat, skin, and hair), plant, fruit, vegetable ...; agricultural, forest, livestock, and fishery products (including processed goods)" among goods to be declared, and "If detected after non-declaration: Imposition of additional tax (40% more than the regular tax)". Added as KCS states it.

entries.old: Canada also advises carrying enough US dollars for your whole stay.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller recommends carrying enough US dollars to cover your whole stay.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct rewrite attributed this to Canada, whose money section says only that notes dated before 2006 are refused; it is Smartraveller that says "It is recommended you carry sufficient funds in US dollars to cover expenses for the duration of your stay."

entries.new: Smartraveller: 999 (police 999 or 777)
entries.note: Audit: 777 confirmed — Canada (updated 28 Sep 2026): "In case of emergency, dial 777." But Smartraveller (updated 22 May 2026) gives "Call 999" for fire and medical and "Call 999 or 777" for police, so the 3 Oct note's 'not given by Canada or the FCDO' left a real conflict unrecorded. Same rank; Canada is newer and wins; Smartraveller recorded in source.conflict.

entries.old: The country remains under do-not-travel advisories from most Western governments.
entries.new: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to South Sudan.
entries.note: Consistency: 'most Western governments' replaced with the three whose advice we read (FCDO, Canada, Smartraveller 'Do not travel'), as the tips and FAQ now say.

entries.old: Most governments advise against all travel to South Sudan due to armed conflict, intercommunal violence, violent crime and kidnapping. The situation can deteriorate quickly, including in Juba, and travel outside the capital requires careful planning and often armed escorts.
entries.new: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to South Sudan. The UK cites the risk of armed violence and criminality; Canada cites armed conflict, inter-ethnic violence, high levels of violent crime and a risk of kidnapping. The UK says the security situation could deteriorate rapidly and unpredictably.
entries.note: Consistency: 'most governments' replaced with the three governments whose advice we read; the armed-escort claim is in no official source we read and was removed.

entries.old: rare

entries.note: Consistency: the payments text (FCDO: cards 'not widely accepted, although some of the newer hotels and supermarkets are starting to'; Canada: 'Credit cards are only accepted in South Sudan in limited locations') describes limited, not rare, acceptance.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says that under the EU's Entry/Exit System you may be asked to give biometric details each time you enter or exit the Schengen area, so allow extra time at the border.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says that under the EU's Entry/Exit System you may be asked to give biometric details every time you enter or exit the Schengen area, and that the checks can take extra time, so allow more time at the border.
entries.note: Audit: WRONG attribution. The "every time you enter or exit" wording is the UK FCDO's ("You may be asked to input biometric details every time you enter or exit"; "be prepared to wait longer than usual at the border"); Canada only says EES "collects information about your trip as well as your facial image and fingerprints" on entry.

entries.old: A passport valid for 6 months, the ETA approval, a confirmed onward or return ticket, and proof of sufficient funds for your stay. Immigration does not always ask for the last two, but airlines can check the ticket at check-in.

entries.old: Sudan has been in full-scale civil war between the armed forces and the RSF since April 2023. Governments uniformly advise against all travel: fighting affects Khartoum, Darfur and much of the country, most embassies have evacuated, and consular help is unavailable.
entries.new: Sudan has been in armed conflict since April 2023. The UK advises against all travel to Sudan (all but essential travel for the Hala'ib Triangle and the Bir Tawil Trapezoid) and Canada says to avoid all travel. The British Embassy in Khartoum is closed, and the UK says it cannot provide in-person consular support inside Sudan.
entries.note: Consistency: Safety text said governments 'uniformly' advise against all travel, that 'most embassies have evacuated' and that consular help is 'unavailable' — not what the cited UK advice says. Rewritten to the UK ('FCDO advises against all travel to Sudan... This does not include the Hala'ib Triangle and the Bir Tawil Trapezoid'; 'The British Embassy in Khartoum is closed') and Canada ('Avoid all travel to Sudan').

entries.old: No — Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Sudan, and evidence of travel to Israel in any passport can also cause refusal.
entries.new: No — Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Sudan. The UK and Canada add that you will be refused entry if your passport contains an Israeli visa or entry or exit stamp.

entries.old: Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Sudan, and evidence of travel to Israel in any passport can also lead to refusal.
entries.new: Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Sudan. The UK and Canada add that any passport containing an Israeli visa or entry or exit stamp is refused entry.

entries.old: Switzerland is not an EU member, but it is part of the Schengen Area through association agreements, so the same short-stay visa rules apply as in the EU Schengen states. It is outside the EU customs union, so customs allowances apply even when arriving from EU neighbors.

For goods, the UK FCDO says there are strict rules about what you can take into and out of Switzerland, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
entries.note: Consistency: the customs-union/allowances claim was withdrawn from entryRequirements.customs.notes as unsourced on 3 Oct but the FAQ still asserted it; replaced with the FCDO's 'There are strict rules about goods that you can take into and out of Switzerland. You must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.'

entries.old: Submit the free online Taiwan Arrival Card within three days before you arrive, through the National Immigration Agency website.
entries.new: Submit the free online Taiwan Arrival Card through the National Immigration Agency's TWAC site, which says to complete it within 7 days before arrival. The UK and Canadian travel advice say within 3 days, so filing in the last 3 days satisfies both.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct change from 7 to 3 days was wrong. The National Immigration Agency's TWAC site (read in headless Chrome) says "Complete and submit within 7 days before arrival." It outranks the UK FCDO and Canada ("within 3 days before arrival"), as the declaration's own source.conflict already records (resolvedBy hierarchy). The tip now matches the declaration and names both windows.

entries.old: Taiwan is one of Asia's safest destinations, with very low crime. The main considerations are natural: typhoons from July to September and occasional earthquakes.
entries.new: Taiwan is one of Asia's safest destinations, with very low crime. The main considerations are natural: typhoons, which the Government of Canada and the UK FCDO say usually occur between May and November, and occasional earthquakes.
entries.note: Consistency: the safety text still gave typhoons "from July to September", which the 3 Oct audit corrected elsewhere to May–November. Canada: "Typhoons usually occur between May and November."

entries.old: (removed on 3 Oct: "Duty-free allowances for adults are 1 liter of alcohol and 200 cigarettes.")
entries.new: Taiwan Customs allows travellers aged 18 or over 1.5 litres of alcohol duty-free, and those aged 20 or over 200 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 1 lb of smoking tobacco. E-cigarettes, e-liquid and heated tobacco products not approved by the Ministry of Health and Welfare are prohibited.
entries.note: Audit: the allowance is officially stated, though not as the withdrawn note had it. Taiwan Customs (Duty Free Exemptions and Payment of Taxes): "A passenger aged 18 or over will be allowed to bring 1.5 liters of alcohol; a passenger aged 20 or over will be allowed to bring 200 cigarettes or 25 cigars or 1lb smoking tobacco"; prohibited: "e-cigarettes, e-liquid, designated tobacco products ... not approved ...". Restored with 1.5 L, not 1 L.

entries.new: Taiwan Customs says inbound passengers may not bring in any fruit: quarantine officers confiscate and destroy it, and the passenger is fined NT$3,000 or more. Almost all animals, plants and their products are prohibited unless a quarantine certificate is presented.
entries.note: Audit: the 3 Oct withdrawal was wrong — Taiwan Customs FAQ: "No, inbound passengers are not allowed to bring any fruits into the country ... passengers will be fined NT$3,000 or more"; and "Almost all animals/plants or the related products are prohibited to carry into by passengers, except that a quarantine certificate is presented." Restored, as the stricter rule Customs states.

entries.old: Yes. Togo requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate from all arriving travelers, and the yellow card is checked on arrival — get vaccinated at least 10 days before your trip.

entries.old: ECOWAS citizens can cross freely. Other nationalities who need a visa must arrive with an approved eVisa, since visas on arrival are suspended.

entries.old: The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May (Canada says November to April), though cyclones can happen at any time, and that whales frequent Tongan waters between June and November. No official source names a best season.
entries.new: The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May (Canada says November to April), though cyclones can happen at any time, and that whales frequent Tongan waters between June and November. entries.old: A confirmed onward or return ticket is required for the visa on arrival, and matters in practice, since Funafuti is served by only a handful of flights a week from Suva.
entries.new: A confirmed onward or return ticket is required for the visa on arrival.

entries.old: Visitors must show sufficient funds and a confirmed place to stay. There are only a few guesthouses and one hotel on Funafuti, so book before you fly and bring the confirmation.
entries.new: Visitors must show sufficient funds and a confirmed place to stay.

entries.new: Every passenger arriving by air or sea, except commercial crew, must complete a paper arrival card (Form 11 of the Immigration Regulations 2014), and a departure card on leaving.

entries.old: Crime is very rare and Funafuti is a small, close-knit community where visitors are quickly known. The real risks are practical: no hospital beyond a basic one, very limited flights, and a low-lying atoll exposed to king tides and storm surge.

The UK government's travel advice says Tuvalu's only hospital is on Funafuti and is adequate for routine treatment, that serious cases may need medical evacuation to Fiji or Australia, and that the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, though cyclones can happen at any time of year.
entries.note: Consistency: the safety text still cited 'very limited flights' (withdrawn on 3 October as unsourced) and described 'no hospital beyond a basic one', which the FCDO contradicts ('Medical facilities are generally adequate for routine medical treatment'). Rewritten from the FCDO health and natural-disasters sections and Canada ('The crime rate is very low. Petty crime occurs.').

entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says credit cards are widely used in cities, but ATMs might not be refilled, some bank cards might not be accepted, and card terminals may not work during power cuts — so carry some hryvnia as well. entries.new: Home country. No entry requirements for Ukrainian citizens; under martial law, Ukrainian and dual-national men aged 23 to 60 are prohibited from leaving the country (UK Foreign Office).

UK FCDO (updated 2 Oct 2026): "Ukrainian national and dual-national males aged 23 to 60 are prohibited from leaving the country." entries.old: Take out travel insurance with medical coverage before you go.

Restored, attributed, matching the travel-insurance text.

entries.old: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires everyone else to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy — often with long interview wait times. Presidential proclamations of June and December 2025 suspend entry on visitor visas for citizens of more than 30 countries, with limited exemptions.
entries.new: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires most other visitors to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy; citizens of the Marshall Islands, Micronesia and Palau, and Bahamians precleared in the Bahamas, also enter without a visa. L. 119-21, s. 100007) — ask the embassy whether it is being charged yet. Requires the DS-160 form and, for most applicants, an in-person interview; appointment wait times vary widely by consulate and can reach several months.

entries.old: Vanuatu is welcoming with low levels of violent crime; petty theft in Port Vila and occasional unrest are the main concerns. Natural hazards are the bigger factor: cyclones from November to April, frequent earthquakes, and active volcanoes on Tanna and Ambrym.
entries.new: Vanuatu is welcoming with low levels of violent crime; petty theft in Port Vila and occasional unrest are the main concerns. Natural hazards are the bigger factor: a cyclone season that normally runs from November to May, frequent earthquakes, and active volcanoes on Tanna, Ambrym and other islands.
entries.note: Consistency: cyclone months aligned with the corrected tip and best-time text — the UK FCDO says the season 'normally runs from November to May'.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says local customs are strictly observed and should be respected, that beachwear should not be worn away from beaches and hotels, and that some kava bars (nakamals), particularly outside Port Vila, do not welcome women. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies.

entries.old: Vatican City has no border controls or visa system of its own. You simply walk in from Rome, so entry is governed entirely by Italy's Schengen rules: EU citizens move freely, around 60 nationalities visit visa-free for 90 days in any 180, and everyone else needs an Italian Schengen visa.
entries.new: Vatican City is reached only through Italy, so Italy's Schengen rules decide who can visit: EU citizens move freely, around 60 nationalities visit visa-free for 90 days in any 180, and everyone else needs an Italian Schengen visa.
entries.note: Consistency: Summary said Vatican City 'has no border controls' and 'you simply walk in from Rome' — the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it). entries.old: Entry is via Italy, so Schengen rules apply: non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond departure from the Schengen Area and issued within the last 10 years. There are no separate Vatican document checks.
entries.new: Entry is via Italy, so Schengen rules apply: non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond departure from the Schengen Area and issued within the last 10 years.
entries.note: Consistency: Still asserted the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it); sentence removed.

entries.old: Travelers who need a Schengen visa for Italy must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it; the Vatican itself checks nothing at its boundary.
entries.new: Travelers who need a Schengen visa for Italy must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it.
entries.note: Consistency: Still asserted the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it); sentence removed.

entries.old: The Vatican performs no border checks. Any onward-travel questions are asked by Italian officers at your point of entry into the Schengen Area.
entries.new: Any onward-travel questions are asked by Italian officers at your point of entry into the Schengen Area.
entries.note: Consistency: Still asserted the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it); sentence removed.

entries.old: No checks at the Vatican boundary. Italy may ask non-EU visitors to show adequate means of support when they enter the Schengen Area.
entries.new: Italy may ask non-EU visitors to show adequate means of support when they enter the Schengen Area.
entries.note: Consistency: Still asserted the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it); sentence removed.

entries.old: The EU rule applies on the way in: cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when entering or leaving the EU. There are no customs controls at the Vatican boundary itself.
entries.new: The EU rule applies on the way in: cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.
entries.note: Consistency: Still asserted the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it); sentence removed.

entries.old: No. Vatican City issues no visas or entry stamps; entry is through Italy, so any Schengen stamp or EES record comes from Italian border control.
entries.new: No official source we read describes a Vatican entry stamp. Entry is through Italy, so any Schengen stamp or EES record comes from the border where you enter the Schengen Area.
entries.note: Consistency: Answer said Vatican City issues no entry stamps — part of the 'no checks at the Vatican boundary' claim withdrawn from the customs notes and tips on 3 Oct (no official source states it).

entries.old: Your allowance is whatever your Schengen status in Italy gives you — for visa-exempt visitors, 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area. In practice the Vatican is a day visit: the basilica, museums and gardens are all doable from Rome.
entries.new: Your allowance is whatever your Schengen status in Italy gives you — for visa-exempt visitors, 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area.
entries.note: Consistency: The 'day visit from Rome' sentence restated the accommodation FAQ withdrawn on 3 Oct (no official source describes staying inside Vatican City); removed.

entries.old: Possibly not. Canada's travel advice says you could be denied entry if your passport bears an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp issued at a crossing with Israel.

entries.old: Many tourists no longer need a visa. SADC citizens enter free, and under a 2023 decree citizens of about 30 major tourism-source countries — including the US, Portugal and most of Western Europe — enter visa-free for up to 30 days. entries.new: Many tourists no longer need a visa. entries.old: All passengers must complete the online Arrival/Departure Card at travel.gov.tt, which opens 72 hours before arrival or departure. Save the receipt with its QR code, printed or on your phone, and show it to officials. You need a valid email address, your flight details, your passport and a JPEG or PNG copy of its bio-data page.
entries.new: All passengers arriving or departing by air or sea must complete the online Arrival/Departure Card at travel.gov.tt; it replaced the paper card on 17 March 2026. The form opens 72 hours before arrival or departure. You create an online account and upload your passport's bio-data page; the portal also asks for a valid email address and your flight details, and takes the bio-data copy as a JPEG or PNG. Save the receipt with its QR code, printed or on your phone, and show it to immigration officials.

entries.new: Mozambique's official eVisa portal sorts visitors into four groups: 17 nationalities, mostly from southern and eastern Africa, are visa-exempt for 30 or 90 days; 29 others, including the US, the UK, Canada, Japan and much of Western Europe, need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) for stays of up to 30 days; citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia must apply at an embassy; and everyone else applies online for an eVisa before travel.

entries.old: Do I need a visa for Mozambique? / Many tourists no longer need a visa. SADC citizens enter free, and under a 2023 decree citizens of about 30 major tourism-source countries — including the US, Portugal and most of Western Europe — enter visa-free for up to 30 days. British and Canadian citizens must first obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online. Most others can get a simplified tourist visa at the border or apply online at evisa.gov.mz, but citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia cannot use the eVisa portal and must apply at a Mozambican embassy.
entries.new: Do I need a visa for Mozambique? / It depends on your passport. Mozambique's official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.mz) lists 17 nationalities, mostly from southern and eastern Africa, as visa-exempt for 30 or 90 days. Citizens of 29 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Portugal and most of Western Europe, need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) before travel, for stays of up to 30 days. Citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia cannot use the portal and must apply at a Mozambican embassy. Everyone else applies online for an eVisa before travelling.
entries.note: Agrees with the rows; foreign advice attributed; unsourced cash-currency claim removed.

entries.old: What is the border fee for visa-free visitors? / Visa-exempt tourists under the 2023 scheme pay a MZN 650 processing fee (about USD 10). Decree 10/2023 sets it as payable when pre-registering at evisa.gov.mz at least 48 hours before boarding, so register and pay online before you fly. Mozambique's High Commission in London describes it as paid on arrival, so carry some cash too — meticais, dollars or rand are normally accepted.
entries.new: Is there a fee for the eTA? / Decree 10/2023, which exempted citizens of about 30 countries from the visa, sets a MZN 650 processing fee, payable when pre-registering at evisa.gov.mz at least 48 hours before boarding; the portal now lists these countries under the eTA scheme. Mozambique's High Commission in London describes the fee as paid on arrival. The UK Foreign Office says British travellers also pay a USD 37 visa fee (about USD 47 in total), online. The portal itself does not publish the eTA fee, so check the amount when you apply.
entries.note: Agrees with the rows; foreign advice attributed; unsourced cash-currency claim removed.

entries.old: Can I get a Mozambique visa on arrival? / Sometimes. Mozambique's border visa allows two entries and 30 days, cannot be extended, and, according to Canada's travel advice, can be paid by card or in accepted currencies (no official source publishes the amount), but the migration service issues it mainly to nationals of countries where Mozambique has no embassy or consulate, or on reciprocity. Applying in advance through evisa.gov.mz is the safer route, especially if you arrive at a small crossing.
entries.new: Can I get a Mozambique visa on arrival? / Only in limited cases. The migration service's visa rules provide a border visa, valid for two entries and 30 days and not extendable, for nationals of countries where Mozambique has no embassy or consulate, or on reciprocity. The official eVisa portal does not offer a visa on arrival: it sorts nationalities into visa-exempt, eTA, eVisa and embassy-only, and tells travellers to carry the printed approval for boarding and arrival. Apply before you travel.
entries.note: Agrees with the rows; foreign advice attributed; unsourced cash-currency claim removed.

entries.new: Every traveller, or the head of a travelling family, entering or leaving Nicaragua must complete a customs Traveller's Declaration. Nicaragua's customs service (DGA) lets you fill it in online and print it, from three days before you travel; it asks, among other things, whether you carry cash or valuables worth USD 10,000 or more.
entries.note: DGA Traveler's Declaration page, read in Chrome: 'ALL TRAVELERS OR HEAD FAMILY TO ENTER OR LEAVE THE COUNTRY MUST COMPLETE A DECLARATION' and 'You can only register your information three days before traveling'. The page does not describe a paper form handed out on flights or the tourist card; the text now says what it states.
